in P_B manifest — no version bump"] 234 235 Start --> Step1 236 Step1 --> Step2 237 Step2 -- "Runtime Edge" --> Step3 238 Step2 -- "Dev / Peer Edge" --> Step4 239 Step3 -- "re-enqueue" --> Step2 240 241 style Start fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a 242 style Step1 fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#4338ca,color:#312e81 243 style Step2 fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#4c1d95 244 style Step3 fill:#d1fae5,stroke:#059669,color:#064e3b 245 style Step4 fill:#fed7aa,stroke:#ea580c,color:#7c2d12 246 ``` 247 248 ### Version Groups (Fixed & Linked) 249 250 `callisto.toml` supports version group rules: 251 - **`[[fixed-group]]`**: All packages in the group are forced to bump in lock-step to the maximum version calculated across any member in the group. 252 - **`[[linked-group]]`**: Packages in the group share severity bumps, but maintain independent base version offsets. 253 254 --- 255 256 ## 7. In-Process VCS Engine (`callisto-vcs`) 257 258 `callisto-vcs` provides Git operations through a dual-backend design: a native `gix` (gitoxide) backend for non-WASM targets, and a `ShellGit` backend that shells out to the real `git` binary for portability and WASM fallback. 259 260 ### Key VCS Capabilities 261 262 - **Repository Discovery**: Walks parent directories from the current working directory to locate `.git` (native backend only; shell backend uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`). 263 - **Commit Walks**: Retrieves commit history to evaluate conventional commits since a given Git ref or release tag. 264 - **Tag Listing**: Matches tags against glob patterns (`v*`, `@scope/*`) using `globset` (both backends apply identical `globset` matching semantics). 265 266 ### Dual-Backend Architecture (`GitAccess`) 267 268 `callisto-vcs` exposes a unified `GitDataSource` trait. The `GitAccess` selector implements it with a deliberate fallback policy: 269 270 - **Read operations** (`list_tags`, `resolve_commit`, `commits_since`): attempt the native `gix` backend first; fall back to `ShellGit` on any error, including failed repo discovery. 271 - **Write operations** (`create_tag`, `create_floating_major`): fall back to `ShellGit` only when native `gix` was unavailable from the start. A discovered repo's result is authoritative — a second backend retry could mask partial mutations. 272 273 ```rust 274 pub struct GitAccess<'r> { 275 native: Option, // None on wasm32 or outside a repo 276 shell: ShellGit<'r>, // always available via CommandRunner 277 } 278 ``` 279 280 ### WASM Target Constraints 281 282 `gix` depends on POSIX signal handlers (`gix-tempfile` -> `signal-hook-registry`), which are unsupported on `wasm32-wasip1`. `GitRepository::discover` always returns `Err` on that target (via a compile-time feature gate), so `GitAccess` automatically routes all operations through `ShellGit`, which calls `git` via the Extism host bridge. 283 284 Note: a 2026 probe confirmed that `gix` object reads fail with `ENOSYS` on WASM even with the signal-hook dependency removed. The shell-git fallback is therefore the production code path for the Moon WASM plugin. 285 286 --- 287 288 ## 8. Extension Architecture & Trait Seams 289 290 Callisto decouples core algorithms from platform-specific I/O using four core trait seams: 291 292 ```rust 293 // 1. Locate workspace project roots 294 pub trait ProjectLocator { 295 fn projects(&self) -> Result, LocateError>; 296 } 297 298 // 2. Command execution abstraction 299 pub trait CommandRunner: Send + Sync { 300 fn run(&self, program: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path) -> Result; 301 302 // Default: delegates to run(). CliCommandRunner overrides with real 303 // spawn + poll + kill so that hung publish commands do not block forever. 304 fn run_with_timeout(&self, program: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path, timeout: Duration) 305 -> Result; 306 } 307 308 // 4. Per-ecosystem manifest reader/writer 309 pub trait Manifest { 310 fn path(&self) -> &Path; 311 fn ecosystem(&self) -> Ecosystem; 312 fn role(&self) -> ManifestRole; 313 fn package_name(&self) -> Result; 314 fn current_version(&self) -> Result; 315 fn write_version(&mut self, new_version: &Version, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>; 316 fn iter_dependencies(&self) -> Box + '_>; 317 fn update_dependency_spec(&mut self, name: &str, new_spec: DepSpec, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>; 318 fn update_optional_dependencies(&mut self, name: &str, new_spec: DepSpec, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>; 319 // publish_targets() and persist() are also required; omitted for brevity. 320 } 321 322 // 5. DependencyResolver supplies graph nodes and edges 323 pub trait DependencyResolver { 324 fn packages(&self) -> impl Iterator; 325 fn dependencies_of(&self, id: &PackageId) -> impl Iterator; 326 fn dependents_of(&self, id: &PackageId) -> impl Iterator; 327 // diagnostics() has a default impl returning an empty slice. 328 } 329 ``` 330 331 ### Moon WASM Plugin Binding (`callisto-moon`) 332 333 `callisto-moon` compiles Callisto into a `wasm32-wasip1` plugin using `extism-pdk`. Moon loads `callisto-moon.wasm` inside Extism, passing host environment queries through Extism FFI exports (`#[plugin_fn]`). 334 335 --- 336 337 ## 9. GitHub Actions Orchestration (`callisto-action`) 338 339 Callisto includes a built-in composite action ([`.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`](.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml)) for CI/CD automation and supports 3 release paradigms (see [`docs/release-paradigms.md`](docs/release-paradigms.md)): 340 341 ```mermaid 342 %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'lineColor': '#64748b', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#f8fafc', 'fontFamily': 'ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif'}}}%% 343 sequenceDiagram 344 participant Runner as GitHub Actions Runner 345 participant Verify as Job 1: verify (Mandatory CI Gate) 346 participant Action as Job 2: release (needs: [verify]) 347 participant CLI as callisto CLI 348 participant GH as GitHub API (gh CLI) 349 350 Runner->>Verify: push / workflow_dispatch 351 Verify->>Verify: format · lint · test · WASM check · cargo-deny audit 352 alt CI Fails 353 Verify-->>Runner: Exit 1 — Job 2 cancelled 354 else CI Passes 355 Verify->>Action: Trigger release job 356 Action->>CLI: callisto status --check 357 alt Pending Changesets 358 Action->>CLI: callisto version 359 Action->>CLI: callisto compose-pr-body 360 Action->>GH: Create or update callisto/version-packages PR 361 else Version PR Merged (zero changesets) 362 Action->>CLI: callisto plan-publish --format json 363 Action->>CLI: callisto publish 364 Action->>CLI: callisto tag --floating-major 365 Action->>GH: Create GitHub Releases & update floating major alias (v1) 366 end 367 end 368 ``` 369 370 ### Complete Action Input Matrix 371 372 | Input | Default | Purpose | 373 | :--- | :--- | :--- | 374 | `publish` | `""` | Command to execute when publishing packages (`cargo publish`, `pnpm publish`, `moon run :publish`). | 375 | `version_command` | `"callisto version"` | Custom versioning command. | 376 | `commit_message` | `"chore: version packages"` | Commit message for the Version Packages PR. | 377 | `title` | `"chore: version packages"` | Pull Request title. | 378 | `pr_label` | `"callisto: release"` | Label automatically attached to the Version Packages PR. | 379 | `create_github_release` | `"true"` | Toggle GitHub Release entry creation for calculated tags. | 380 | `setup_git_user` | `"true"` | Automatically configure `git config user.name` & `user.email` bot credentials. | 381 | `branch` | `"main"` | Base branch for Version PRs. | 382 | `cwd` | `"."` | Working directory path if workspace root is nested in a subfolder. | 383 384 ### Diagnostic Problem Matchers & Toolchain Isolation 385 386 - **Inline PR Annotations**: Registered [`.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json`](.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json) in `setup-callisto`. Automatically highlights invalid `.changeset/*.md` syntax or missing package IDs as inline callouts on PR diff lines. 387 - **Pre-installed Toolchain Targets**: All toolchain setup steps declare `targets: wasm32-wasip1` up-front alongside `rustfmt` and `clippy`. This prevents parallel `rustup` download race conditions when Moon executes 10 crate tasks in parallel. 388 - **Unbuffered Stream Output & UI Accordions**: Long-running shell commands use `::group::` and `::endgroup::` annotations for foldable UI accordions, streaming stdout and stderr live to the runner console. 389 390 --- 391 392 ## 10. PR Pre-Flight Verification & Local Git Hooks 393 394 ### PR Pre-Flight Verification (`callisto-validate`) 395 396 Every Pull Request runs the standalone [`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) action: 397 1. **Package Discovery Guard**: Verifies all workspace crates and packages are accounted for in `callisto.toml`. 398 2. **Schema & Config Health**: Validates `callisto.toml` fields and types. 399 3. **Changeset Syntax Integrity**: Verifies `.changeset/*.md` frontmatter and package IDs. 400 4. **Pre-Flight Release Simulation**: Simulates `callisto plan-publish` topological DAG sorting to ensure zero cyclic dependencies before PR merge. 401 402 ### Ultra-Fast Local Git Hooks (`pre-commit` & `pre-push`) 403 404 Callisto standardizes local developer hook workflows in [`justfile`](justfile): 405 - `just pre-commit` (~100ms): Fast formatting check before local commits. 406 - `just pre-push` (~1.5s): Formatting check and Clippy lints before remote pushes. 407 - `just hooks`: Installs native `.git/hooks/pre-commit` and `.git/hooks/pre-push` shell scripts in one command. 408 409 --- 410 411 ## 11. Engineering Invariants & Quality Controls 412 413 All contributions to Callisto must adhere to the following 4 engineering invariants: 414 415 1. **Safe Rust Strictness**: `unsafe_code = "forbid"` is enforced across all 10 workspace crates. 416 2. **Zero Clippy Warnings**: Code must compile with zero warnings under `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`. 417 3. **Format Enforcement**: Code formatting must strictly match `cargo fmt --check`. 418 4. **Comprehensive Test Suite Coverage**: Unit, integration, doctests, and lifecycle E2E tests must pass (`just ci`). 419 420 --- 421 422 ## 12. Zero-Config Multi-Platform Native Matrix Auto-Discovery (`callisto matrix`) [partially implemented] 423 424 > **Status: napi-rs and maturin platform-target discovery, plus npm/PyPI runtime-version constraints, are implemented** (`callisto matrix [--package ]`, `--format text|json` via the global flag). Java (JNI) target discovery, .NET native-AOT target discovery, and the `callisto publish-target` subcommand described later in this section remain unimplemented and are planned for a future release. 425 426 To eliminate configuration duplication and configuration drift across native Rust, NAPI-RS, Maturin (Python), and Java (JNI) polyglot monorepos, `callisto matrix` provides dynamic matrix auto-discovery: 427 428 ```text 429 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ 430 │ CALLISTO NATIVE MATRIX AUTO-DISCOVERY │ 431 ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ 432 │ Workspace Manifests (Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml) │ 433 │ ↳ Single Source of Truth: napi.triplets, maturin.targets, engines │ 434 ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ 435 │ callisto matrix --format json │ 436 │ ↳ Dynamically computes runner OS, target triples, & runtime versions │ 437 ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ 438 │ GitHub Actions / GitLab CI Job Matrix │ 439 │ ↳ Parallel native build matrix execution without hardcoded YAML arrays │ 440 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 441 ``` 442 443 ### Manifest-Driven Target Auto-Detection 444 445 1. **NAPI-RS (`package.json`)**: Auto-detects `napi.triplets` (e.g. `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) and maps them to GitHub Actions runner OS (`ubuntu-latest`, `macos-14`, `windows-latest`). 446 2. **Maturin (`pyproject.toml`)**: Auto-detects `tool.maturin.targets` and Python runtime compatibility bounds. 447 3. **Runtime Engine Compatibility**: Automatically extracts Node.js (`engines.node`) and Java (`java.version` / `pom.xml`) versions directly from package manifests, eliminating duplicate version strings in CI YAML. 448 449 ### Zero-Config GitHub Actions Workflow Pattern 450 451 ```yaml 452 jobs: 453 matrix: 454 runs-on: ubuntu-latest 455 outputs: 456 matrix: ${{ steps.discover.outputs.matrix }} 457 steps: 458 - uses: actions/checkout@v4 459 - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto 460 - id: discover 461 run: echo "matrix=$(callisto matrix --format json)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT 462 463 build: 464 needs: matrix 465 strategy: 466 matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.matrix.outputs.matrix) }} 467 runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }} 468 steps: 469 - uses: actions/checkout@v4 470 - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto 471 - run: callisto publish-target --package ${{ matrix.package }} --target ${{ matrix.target }} 472 ``` 473 474 --- 475 476 ## 13. Hermetic Build Systems & Custom Orchestration (Bazel, Buck2, Nix, GitLab CI) 477 478 Callisto's core engine is decoupled from GitHub Actions. All versioning, status calculation, and dependency graph sorting execute as pure, hermetic CLI subcommands that operate on filesystem inputs and emit standard JSON/Text data streams. 479 480 ```text 481 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ 482 │ HERMETIC & ENGINE-AGNOSTIC CALLISTO ARCHITECTURE │ 483 ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ 484 │ Callisto Engine (crates/callisto-cli & callisto-graph) │ 485 │ ↳ Pure Rust, Hermetic Input Ingestion, Zero GitHub API Hardcoding │ 486 ├───────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┤ 487 │ CLI / BUILD SYSTEM INTERFACE │ OUTPUT FORMAT │ 488 ├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤ 489 │ callisto plan-publish │ Hermetic JSON │ 490 │ callisto status │ Struct/JSON workspace state │ 491 │ callisto tag │ Native Git refs or build outputs │ 492 │ callisto matrix │ Standard JSON array for any runner │ 493 └───────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘ 494 ``` 495 496 ### Bazel Integration Pattern (`rules_callisto`) 497 498 In Bazel (`BUILD.bazel`), Callisto operates as a hermetic toolchain binary: 499 500 ```starlark 501 load("@rules_callisto//callisto:defs.bzl", "callisto_release_plan", "callisto_version_check") 502 503 # Hermetic changeset validation rule in Bazel build graph 504 callisto_version_check( 505 name = "changeset_validation_test", 506 srcs = glob([".changeset/*.md", "**/Cargo.toml", "**/package.json"]), 507 ) 508 509 # Output target producing topological release plan for downstream Bazel actions 510 callisto_release_plan( 511 name = "release_plan", 512 srcs = glob(["**/*"]), 513 out = "release_plan.json", 514 ) 515 ``` 516 517 ### Guarantees for Non-GitHub Environments 518 519 1. **Zero Network / API Lock-in**: `callisto status`, `callisto plan-publish`, and `callisto matrix` operate entirely on local workspace files and write to stdout/JSON. They run identically inside Bazel sandboxes, Nix flakes, GitLab CI, Buildkite, and Jenkins. 520 2. **Hermetic File Inputs**: Accepts explicit `--cwd` and `--config` overrides to run inside isolated build tool sandboxes without relying on global environment variables. 521 3. **Thin Adapter Seams**: GitHub Actions ([`callisto-action`](.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml)), Moon WASM ([`callisto-moon`](crates/callisto-moon)), and Bazel (`rules_callisto`) are thin adapter layers wrapping the same core Rust CLI engine. 522 523 --- 524 525 ## 14. Multi-Phase Polyglot Master Specification & Architecture Roadmap 526 527 Callisto is engineered to support polyglot monorepos across **Rust, TypeScript/JS, Python, Go, Java (Maven/Gradle), and C# (.NET)** through a unified, 4-phase architectural roadmap. 528 529 ```text 530 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ 531 │ CALLISTO MULTI-PHASE POLYGLOT ARCHITECTURE ROADMAP │ 532 ├─────────┬─────────────────┬───────────────────┬────────────────────────┤ 533 │ PHASE │ ECOSYSTEM │ MANIFEST & FORMAT │ VERSION DRIVER & SPEC │ 534 ├─────────┼─────────────────┼───────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ 535 │ Phase 1 │ Python │ pyproject.toml │ ManifestField │ 536 │ │ (Implemented) │ (toml_edit CST) │ PEP 440 (pep440_rs) │ 537 ├─────────┼─────────────────┼───────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ 538 │ Phase 2 │ Go │ go.mod / go.work │ GitTag │ 539 │ │ (Specified) │ (modfile AST) │ SemVer 2.0.0 (vX.Y.Z) │ 540 ├─────────┼─────────────────┼───────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ 541 │ Phase 3 │ Java │ pom.xml / gradle │ ManifestField / Prop │ 542 │ │ (Specified) │ (xmltree CST) │ Maven (Qualifiers) │ 543 ├─────────┼─────────────────┼───────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ 544 │ Phase 4 │ C# / .NET │ *.csproj / CPM │ ManifestField │ 545 │ │ (Specified) │ (xmltree CST) │ NuGet SemVer │ 546 └─────────┴─────────────────┴───────────────────┴────────────────────────┘ 547 ``` 548 549 ### Ecosystem Implementation Status Legend 550 551 - **`[LIVE: IMPLEMENTED]`**: Fully compiled, tested, and active in the Rust workspace today. 552 - **`[PLANNED: SPECIFIED]`**: Architecturally specified in `docs/` and ready for implementation in future phases. 553 554 ### Phase 1: Python Engine (`pyproject.toml` / PyPI) — **STATUS: [LIVE: IMPLEMENTED]** 555 - Callisto Architecture & Engineering Specification

Authoritative specification for crate topography, graph algorithms, format preservation, and CI orchestration.

--- ## 1. Executive Architecture & Strategic Invariants Callisto addresses key architectural deficiencies in existing release management tools: - **Runtime Performance**: Replaces heavy JavaScript/Node.js runtimes (`@changesets/cli`) with an optimized native Rust engine that completes status, versioning, and graph operations in `<10ms`. - **AST Format Preservation**: Replaces destructive text/regex search-and-replace with concrete syntax tree (CST) editors (`toml_edit` and `serde_json` with indentation fingerprinting), preserving comments, table order, and whitespace. - **Crash-Safe File Mutations**: Enforces atomic filesystem transactions using temporary directory file swaps (`NamedTempFile` + `fs::rename`) to prevent half-written or corrupt manifests during unexpected process termination. - **In-Process Git Engine**: Eliminates external `git` subprocess spawns by leveraging `gix` (gitoxide) for fast, thread-safe repository discovery, commit traversal, and ref resolution. - **Formal Graph Solver**: Constructs a directed acyclic graph (DAG) using `petgraph`, executing Tarjan's Strongly Connected Components (SCC) algorithm to detect circular dependencies before applying topological version cascades. - **Dual Licensing Isolation**: Separates permissive data types (`MIT/Apache-2.0`) from copyleft execution logic (`AGPL-3.0`), allowing third-party tools to consume Callisto's domain contracts without importing AGPL code. --- ## 2. System Architecture & Pipeline Data Flow Callisto processes monorepo release workflows through a deterministic 5-stage pipeline: ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'lineColor': '#64748b', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#f8fafc', 'fontFamily': 'ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif'}}}%% flowchart TB subgraph Stage1 ["Stage 1 — Discovery & Identity"] PL(["ProjectLocator
(IgnoreWalk / Moon)"]) --> IR(["IdentityResolver
(Canonical PackageId)"]) end subgraph Stage2 ["Stage 2 — Manifest & VCS Ingestion"] IR --> MR(["Manifest Reader
(Cargo / npm / pyproject)"]) IR --> VCS(["callisto-vcs
(gix In-Process Git Engine)"]) end subgraph Stage3 ["Stage 3 — Graph Construction & Cycle Detection"] MR --> DAG(["callisto-graph
(petgraph DiGraph)"]) VCS --> DAG DAG --> SCC{"Tarjan SCC
Cycle Check"} SCC -- "Cycle Detected" --> Err(["Emit miette
Diagnostic Card"]) SCC -- "Acyclic" --> Agg(["Aggregate Changesets
& Conventional Commits"]) end subgraph Stage4 ["Stage 4 — Cascade & Plan Generation"] Agg --> Cascade(["Cascade Propagation Engine
(Runtime / Dev / Peer Edge Rules)"]) Cascade --> Plan(["VersionPlan Construction
(Calculated Version Bumps)"]) end subgraph Stage5 ["Stage 5 — Format-Preserving Persistence"] Plan --> Diff(["Render Unified Diffs"]) Plan --> AST(["CST Rewrite
(toml_edit / serde_json)"]) AST --> Atomic(["Atomic Persistence
(NamedTempFile + fs::rename)"]) end style Stage1 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,stroke-width:2px,color:#1e3a8a style Stage2 fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#4338ca,stroke-width:2px,color:#312e81 style Stage3 fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,stroke-width:2px,color:#4c1d95 style Stage4 fill:#d1fae5,stroke:#059669,stroke-width:2px,color:#064e3b style Stage5 fill:#fed7aa,stroke:#ea580c,stroke-width:2px,color:#7c2d12 ``` --- ## 3. (Format-Preserving Editors)"]) VCS(["callisto-vcs

| Layer | Responsibility | Key Dependencies | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `callisto-model` | MIT/Apache-2.0 | Layer 1 | Core domain primitives, version grammars, JSON report schemas, atomic disk writes | `semver`, `schemars`, `serde`, `tempfile` | | `callisto-format` | MIT/Apache-2.0 | Layer 1 | Byte-compatible parser and writer for changeset `.md` and `pre.json` | `indexmap`, `serde` | | `callisto-conventional` | AGPL-3.0 | Layer 1 | Conventional commit parsing and severity classification | `thiserror` | | `callisto-changelog` | AGPL-3.0 | Layer 1 | Sectioned Markdown changelog rendering | `pulldown-cmark` | | `callisto-manifests` | AGPL-3.0 | Layer 2 | Format-preserving manifest AST editing and atomic writes | `toml_edit`, `serde_json`, `tempfile` | | `callisto-vcs` | MIT/Apache-2.0 | Layer 2 | Git operations via `gix` (native, non-wasm32) with `ShellGit` fallback | `gix`, `globset` | | `callisto-graph` | AGPL-3.0 | Layer 3 | Dependency DAG construction, Tarjan SCC cycle detection, cascade engine | `petgraph`, `ignore` | | `callisto-cli` | AGPL-3.0 | Layer 4 | Standalone CLI binary, colored diff previews, `miette` error reporting | `clap`, `miette`, `anstream`, `similar` | | `callisto-moon` | AGPL-3.0 | Layer 4 | Moon extension host integration and WASM compilation target | `extism-pdk` (`wasm32-wasip1`) | | `callisto-fixtures` | AGPL-3.0 | Dev | Multi-ecosystem corpus and in-memory test doubles | Dev-only test helpers | --- ## 4. Formal Domain Model & Type System Callisto defines type-safe primitives in `callisto-model` to prevent stringly-typed bugs across ecosystem boundaries: ### Core Domain Primitives - `PackageId(String)`: Unique canonical identity for a workspace package (e.g. `callisto-cli` or `@myorg/web-app`). - `Version`: SemVer version wrapper (`semver::Version`) enforcing SemVer 2.0.0 specification rules. - `Severity`: Bumping magnitude enum (`None < Patch < Minor < Major`). Implements `Ord` to allow computing maximum required severity across multiple changesets. - `Changeset`: Representation of a `.changeset/.md` document: ```rust pub struct Changeset { pub id: String, pub releases: IndexMap, pub summary: String, } ``` - `PreState`: Model for `.changeset/pre.json` managing pre-release modes (e.g. `alpha`, `beta`, `rc`): ```rust pub struct PreState { pub mode: PreMode, // Enter | Exit pub tag: String, pub initial_versions: IndexMap, pub changesets: Vec, } ``` --- ## 5. Manifest Parsing & Atomic Mutation Mechanics Callisto guarantees that editing package manifests (`Cargo.toml`, `package.json`) never corrupts file formatting or damages unmanaged sections. ### Concrete Syntax Tree (CST) Editing for `Cargo.toml` `callisto-manifests` uses `toml_edit` to parse `Cargo.toml` into a Concrete Syntax Tree. This ensures: - Header comments, inline comments, and section spacing are preserved exactly. - Key ordering within tables remains untouched. - Version string updates target only the specific `[package].version` item or path dependency tables (`[dependencies.crate-name].version`). ### Indentation Fingerprinting for `package.json` JSON specifications do not preserve formatting. `callisto-manifests` addresses this by fingerprinting `package.json` before parsing: 1. Scans line prefixes to determine indentation style (`IndentStyle::Tabs` vs `IndentStyle::Spaces(usize)`). 2. Parses the document using `serde_json` with `preserve_order` enabled to preserve key insertion order. 3. Serializes updated documents using a custom formatter matching the fingerprinted indentation style and line endings (`LF` vs `CRLF`). ### Atomic Disk Persistence (`atomic_write`) To guarantee crash-safety during file writes: ```rust pub fn atomic_write(path: &Path, content: &str, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> io::Result<()> { let parent_dir = path.parent().ok_or(...)?; let mut temp_file = NamedTempFile::new_in(parent_dir)?; temp_file.write_all(content.as_bytes())?; temp_file.as_file().sync_all()?; temp_file.persist(path)?; // fsync parent and grandparent directories for durability after rename. sync_dir(parent_dir)?; if let Some(grandparent) = parent_dir.parent() { sync_dir(grandparent)?; } Ok(()) } ``` `ApplyPermit` is a capability token that must be obtained before any mutating operation (see §7). By creating `NamedTempFile` in the same directory as the target file, the final `fs::rename` is an atomic OS kernel operation on POSIX and Windows filesystems. Parent and grandparent directory fsyncs ensure the rename is durable on power-loss. --- ## 6. Dependency DAG Engine & Algorithmic Complexities Workspace package relationships form a directed graph `G = (V, E)` where vertices $V$ represent `PackageId` nodes and edges $E$ represent dependency declarations. ### Topological Sorting & Cycle Diagnostics 1. **Graph Construction**: `callisto-graph` builds a `petgraph::graph::DiGraph`. 2. **Cycle Detection (Tarjan's SCC Algorithm)**: - Before calculating version bumps, `callisto-graph` executes Tarjan's Strongly Connected Components algorithm ($O(|V| + |E|)$ time, $O(|V|)$ space). - If circular dependencies exist (e.g. $A \to B \to C \to A$), Callisto isolates the exact cycle path and formats a colorized `miette` diagnostic card: ```text Error: Circular dependency cycle detected in workspace graph callisto-graph → callisto-manifests → callisto-graph Tip: Refactor shared types into a common Layer 1 crate or mark peer dependencies. ``` 3. **Topological Order Execution**: - Executes Kahn's algorithm ($O(|V| + |E|)$) to establish linear build and publish ordering. ### Bump Cascade Engine When a package $P_A$ is bumped from version $V_{old}$ to $V_{new}$ with severity $S$: ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'lineColor': '#64748b', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#f8fafc', 'fontFamily': 'ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif'}}}%% flowchart TD Start(["Input: Package P_A
with Severity S"]) Step1["Apply severity S to P_A
Calculate V_new"] Step2{"Inspect Reverse
Dependencies of P_A"} Step3["Calculate required bump for P_B
Re-enqueue (P_B, derived severity)"] Step4["Update dependency range
in P_B manifest — no version bump"] Start --> Step1 Step1 --> Step2 Step2 -- "Runtime Edge" --> Step3 Step2 -- "Dev / Peer Edge" --> Step4 Step3 -- "re-enqueue" --> Step2 style Start fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a style Step1 fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#4338ca,color:#312e81 style Step2 fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#4c1d95 style Step3 fill:#d1fae5,stroke:#059669,color:#064e3b style Step4 fill:#fed7aa,stroke:#ea580c,color:#7c2d12 ``` ### Version Groups (Fixed & Linked) `callisto.toml` supports version group rules: - **`[[fixed-group]]`**: All packages in the group are forced to bump in lock-step to the maximum version calculated across any member in the group. - **`[[linked-group]]`**: Packages in the group share severity bumps, but maintain independent base version offsets. --- ## 7. In-Process VCS Engine (`callisto-vcs`) `callisto-vcs` provides Git operations through a dual-backend design: a native `gix` (gitoxide) backend for non-WASM targets, and a `ShellGit` backend that shells out to the real `git` binary for portability and WASM fallback. ### Key VCS Capabilities - **Repository Discovery**: Walks parent directories from the current working directory to locate `.git` (native backend only; shell backend uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`). - **Commit Walks**: Retrieves commit history to evaluate conventional commits since a given Git ref or release tag. - **Tag Listing**: Matches tags against glob patterns (`v*`, `@scope/*`) using `globset` (both backends apply identical `globset` matching semantics). ### Dual-Backend Architecture (`GitAccess`) `callisto-vcs` exposes a unified `GitDataSource` trait. The `GitAccess` selector implements it with a deliberate fallback policy: - **Read operations** (`list_tags`, `resolve_commit`, `commits_since`): attempt the native `gix` backend first; fall back to `ShellGit` on any error, including failed repo discovery. - **Write operations** (`create_tag`, `create_floating_major`): fall back to `ShellGit` only when native `gix` was unavailable from the start. A discovered repo's result is authoritative — a second backend retry could mask partial mutations. ```rust pub struct GitAccess<'r> { native: Option, // None on wasm32 or outside a repo shell: ShellGit<'r>, // always available via CommandRunner } ``` ### WASM Target Constraints `gix` depends on POSIX signal handlers (`gix-tempfile` -> `signal-hook-registry`), which are unsupported on `wasm32-wasip1`. `GitRepository::discover` always returns `Err` on that target (via a compile-time feature gate), so `GitAccess` automatically routes all operations through `ShellGit`, which calls `git` via the Extism host bridge. Note: a 2026 probe confirmed that `gix` object reads fail with `ENOSYS` on WASM even with the signal-hook dependency removed. The shell-git fallback is therefore the production code path for the Moon WASM plugin. --- ## 8. Extension Architecture & Trait Seams Callisto decouples core algorithms from platform-specific I/O using four core trait seams: ```rust // 1. Locate workspace project roots pub trait ProjectLocator { fn projects(&self) -> Result, LocateError>; } // 2. Command execution abstraction pub trait CommandRunner: Send + Sync { fn run(&self, program: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path) -> Result; // Default: delegates to run(). CliCommandRunner overrides with real // spawn + poll + kill so that hung publish commands do not block forever. fn run_with_timeout(&self, program: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path, timeout: Duration) -> Result; } // 4. Per-ecosystem manifest reader/writer pub trait Manifest { fn path(&self) -> &Path; fn ecosystem(&self) -> Ecosystem; fn role(&self) -> ManifestRole; fn package_name(&self) -> Result; fn current_version(&self) -> Result; fn write_version(&mut self, new_version: &Version, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>; fn iter_dependencies(&self) -> Box + '_>; fn update_dependency_spec(&mut self, name: &str, new_spec: DepSpec, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>; fn update_optional_dependencies(&mut self, name: &str, new_spec: DepSpec, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>; // publish_targets() and persist() are also required; omitted for brevity. } // 5. DependencyResolver supplies graph nodes and edges pub trait DependencyResolver { fn packages(&self) -> impl Iterator; fn dependencies_of(&self, id: &PackageId) -> impl Iterator; fn dependents_of(&self, id: &PackageId) -> impl Iterator; // diagnostics() has a default impl returning an empty slice. } ``` ### Moon WASM Plugin Binding (`callisto-moon`) `callisto-moon` compiles Callisto into a `wasm32-wasip1` plugin using `extism-pdk`. Moon loads `callisto-moon.wasm` inside Extism, passing host environment queries through Extism FFI exports (`#[plugin_fn]`). --- ## 9. GitHub Actions Orchestration (`callisto-action`) Callisto includes a built-in composite action ([`.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`](.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml)) for CI/CD automation and supports 3 release paradigms (see [`docs/release-paradigms.md`](docs/release-paradigms.md)): ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'lineColor': '#64748b', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#f8fafc', 'fontFamily': 'ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif'}}}%% sequenceDiagram participant Runner as GitHub Actions Runner participant Verify as Job 1: verify (Mandatory CI Gate) participant Action as Job 2: release (needs: [verify]) participant CLI as callisto CLI participant GH as GitHub API (gh CLI) Runner->>Verify: push / workflow_dispatch Verify->>Verify: format · lint · test · WASM check · cargo-deny audit alt CI Fails Verify-->>Runner: Exit 1 — Job 2 cancelled else CI Passes Verify->>Action: Trigger release job Action->>CLI: callisto status --check alt Pending Changesets Action->>CLI: callisto version Action->>CLI: callisto compose-pr-body Action->>GH: Create or update callisto/version-packages PR else Version PR Merged (zero changesets) Action->>CLI: callisto plan-publish --format json Action->>CLI: callisto publish Action->>CLI: callisto tag --floating-major Action->>GH: Create GitHub Releases & update floating major alias (v1) end end ``` ### Complete Action Input Matrix | Input | Default | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `publish` | `""` | Command to execute when publishing packages (`cargo publish`, `pnpm publish`, `moon run :publish`). | | `version_command` | `"callisto version"` | Custom versioning command. | | `commit_message` | `"chore: version packages"` | Commit message for the Version Packages PR. | | `title` | `"chore: version packages"` | Pull Request title. | | `pr_label` | `"callisto: release"` | Label automatically attached to the Version Packages PR. | | `create_github_release` | `"true"` | Toggle GitHub Release entry creation for calculated tags. | | `setup_git_user` | `"true"` | Automatically configure `git config user.name` & `user.email` bot credentials. | | `branch` | `"main"` | Base branch for Version PRs. | | `cwd` | `"."` | Working directory path if workspace root is nested in a subfolder. | ### Diagnostic Problem Matchers & Toolchain Isolation - **Inline PR Annotations**: Registered [`.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json`](.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json) in `setup-callisto`. Automatically highlights invalid `.changeset/*.md` syntax or missing package IDs as inline callouts on PR diff lines. - **Pre-installed Toolchain Targets**: All toolchain setup steps declare `targets: wasm32-wasip1` up-front alongside `rustfmt` and `clippy`. This prevents parallel `rustup` download race conditions when Moon executes 10 crate tasks in parallel. - **Unbuffered Stream Output & UI Accordions**: Long-running shell commands use `::group::` and `::endgroup::` annotations for foldable UI accordions, streaming stdout and stderr live to the runner console. --- ## 10. PR Pre-Flight Verification & Local Git Hooks ### PR Pre-Flight Verification (`callisto-validate`) Every Pull Request runs the standalone [`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) action: 1. **Package Discovery Guard**: Verifies all workspace crates and packages are accounted for in `callisto.toml`. 2. **Schema & Config Health**: Validates `callisto.toml` fields and types. 3. **Changeset Syntax Integrity**: Verifies `.changeset/*.md` frontmatter and package IDs. 4. **Pre-Flight Release Simulation**: Simulates `callisto plan-publish` topological DAG sorting to ensure zero cyclic dependencies before PR merge. ### Ultra-Fast Local Git Hooks (`pre-commit` & `pre-push`) Callisto standardizes local developer hook workflows in [`justfile`](justfile): - `just pre-commit` (~100ms): Fast formatting check before local commits. - `just pre-push` (~1.5s): Formatting check and Clippy lints before remote pushes. - `just hooks`: Installs native `.git/hooks/pre-commit` and `.git/hooks/pre-push` shell scripts in one command. --- ## 11. Engineering Invariants & Quality Controls All contributions to Callisto must adhere to the following 4 engineering invariants: 1. **Safe Rust Strictness**: `unsafe_code = "forbid"` is enforced across all 10 workspace crates. 2. **Zero Clippy Warnings**: Code must compile with zero warnings under `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`. 3. **Format Enforcement**: Code formatting must strictly match `cargo fmt --check`. 4. **Comprehensive Test Suite Coverage**: Unit, integration, doctests, and lifecycle E2E tests must pass (`just ci`). --- ## 12. Zero-Config Multi-Platform Native Matrix Auto-Discovery (`callisto matrix`) [partially implemented] > **Status: napi-rs and maturin platform-target discovery, plus npm/PyPI runtime-version constraints, are implemented** (`callisto matrix [--package ]`, `--format text|json` via the global flag). Java (JNI) target discovery, .NET native-AOT target discovery, and the `callisto publish-target` subcommand described later in this section remain unimplemented and are planned for a future release. To eliminate configuration duplication and configuration drift across native Rust, NAPI-RS, Maturin (Python), and Java (JNI) polyglot monorepos, `callisto matrix` provides dynamic matrix auto-discovery: ```text ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ CALLISTO NATIVE MATRIX AUTO-DISCOVERY │ ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Workspace Manifests (Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml) │ │ ↳ Single Source of Truth: napi.triplets, maturin.targets, engines │ ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ callisto matrix --format json │ │ ↳ Dynamically computes runner OS, target triples, & runtime versions │ ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ GitHub Actions / GitLab CI Job Matrix │ │ ↳ Parallel native build matrix execution without hardcoded YAML arrays │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### Manifest-Driven Target Auto-Detection 1. **NAPI-RS (`package.json`)**: Auto-detects `napi.triplets` (e.g. `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) and maps them to GitHub Actions runner OS (`ubuntu-latest`, `macos-14`, `windows-latest`). 2. **Maturin (`pyproject.toml`)**: Auto-detects `tool.maturin.targets` and Python runtime compatibility bounds. 3. **Runtime Engine Compatibility**: Automatically extracts Node.js (`engines.node`) and Java (`java.version` / `pom.xml`) versions directly from package manifests, eliminating duplicate version strings in CI YAML. ### Zero-Config GitHub Actions Workflow Pattern ```yaml jobs: matrix: runs-on: ubuntu-latest outputs: matrix: ${{ steps.discover.outputs.matrix }} steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto - id: discover run: echo "matrix=$(callisto matrix --format json)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT build: needs: matrix strategy: matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.matrix.outputs.matrix) }} runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }} steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto - run: callisto publish-target --package ${{ matrix.package }} --target ${{ matrix.target }} ``` --- ## 13. Hermetic Build Systems & Custom Orchestration (Bazel, Buck2, Nix, GitLab CI) Callisto's core engine is decoupled from GitHub Actions. All versioning, status calculation, and dependency graph sorting execute as pure, hermetic CLI subcommands that operate on filesystem inputs and emit standard JSON/Text data streams. ```text ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ HERMETIC & ENGINE-AGNOSTIC CALLISTO ARCHITECTURE │ ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Callisto Engine (crates/callisto-cli & callisto-graph) │ │ ↳ Pure Rust, Hermetic Input Ingestion, Zero GitHub API Hardcoding │ ├───────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┤ │ CLI / BUILD SYSTEM INTERFACE │ OUTPUT FORMAT │ ├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤ │ callisto plan-publish │ Hermetic JSON │ │ callisto status │ Struct/JSON workspace state │ │ callisto tag │ Native Git refs or build outputs │ │ callisto matrix │ Standard JSON array for any runner │ └───────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### Bazel Integration Pattern (`rules_callisto`) In Bazel (`BUILD.bazel`), Callisto operates as a hermetic toolchain binary: ```starlark load("@rules_callisto//callisto:defs.bzl", "callisto_release_plan", "callisto_version_check") # Hermetic changeset validation rule in Bazel build graph callisto_version_check( name = "changeset_validation_test", srcs = glob([".changeset/*.md", "**/Cargo.toml", "**/package.json"]), ) # Output target producing topological release plan for downstream Bazel actions callisto_release_plan( name = "release_plan", srcs = glob(["**/*"]), out = "release_plan.json", ) ``` ### Guarantees for Non-GitHub Environments 1. **Zero Network / API Lock-in**: `callisto status`, `callisto plan-publish`, and `callisto matrix` operate entirely on local workspace files and write to stdout/JSON. They run identically inside Bazel sandboxes, Nix flakes, GitLab CI, Buildkite, and Jenkins. 2. **Hermetic File Inputs**: Accepts explicit `--cwd` and `--config` overrides to run inside isolated build tool sandboxes without relying on global environment variables. 3. **Thin Adapter Seams**: GitHub Actions ([`callisto-action`](.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml)), Moon WASM ([`callisto-moon`](crates/callisto-moon)), and Bazel (`rules_callisto`) are thin adapter layers wrapping the same core Rust CLI engine. --- ## 14. ## Context

This is a follow-up fix in a larger task that already redacted subprocess-stderr-into-error leaks at 4 other sites across 3 crates (callisto-graph's apply.rs/commands/validate.rs, callisto-vcs's shell.rs, callisto-conventional's pre_cursor.rs) — each using the same pattern: a local `redact_git_stderr(text) -> String` wrapping `callisto_model::redact_known_secrets(text, &callisto_model::known_credential_env_values(std::env::vars()))`, applied before embedding raw `git` subprocess stderr into a displayed/serialized error type. The fix: extracted the git-add-and-check logic out of the inline `handle()` body into a new private function `fn stage_pre_json(runner: &dyn CommandRunner, root: &Path) -> Result<(), CliError>`, added a local `redact_git_stderr` helper (mirroring the other 4 crates' copies), wired `redact_git_stderr(&output.stderr)` into the error-construction site inside `stage_pre_json`, and added a new `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (this file previously had none) with one test using a fake `CommandRunner` returning a GitHub-Actions-shaped credential-bearing stderr, asserting the resulting `CliError`'s rendered text doesn't contain the raw secret and does contain `[REDACTED]`. `handle()`'s call site was changed from ~9 lines of inline git-add-and-check logic to a single `stage_pre_json(&runner, &ws.root)?;` call.

The fix author manually verified the test is non-tautological via a temporary mutation (reverting `redact_git_stderr(&output.stderr)` to `output.stderr.clone()`, confirming the test fails, then restoring the fix) — you don't need to repeat that, but you may spot-check it if you want extra confidence.

input.description: Verify IdentityIndex.platform wiring fix
input.prompt:
You are reviewing an uncommitted change to the Callisto Rust workspace at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto, spanning `crates/callisto-graph/src/identity.rs`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`, and `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs`. Run `git diff -- crates/callisto-graph/src/identity.rs crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs` to see the exact changes. Do not trust any summary from me — read the diff and current source yourself, and be skeptical: this fix required unusually deep architectural investigation before being written, which is exactly the kind of situation where a subtle mistake is easy to miss.

## Background — what was broken and why

`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`'s workspace-discovery loop already detected napi platform npm packages (via `detect_npm_role`, which reads a `package.json`'s `os`/`cpu` fields) and pushed a `ManifestDecl` with `ManifestRole::Platform` into a package's manifest list (used for publish routing). But it never inserted anything into `IdentityIndex.platform` — a `BTreeMap` that `crate::config::groups::GroupTable::resolve` consults as a fallback when a `[[fixed-group]]`/`[[linked-group]]` config's `members` list names something that doesn't resolve to a real registered `Package` (i.e. a platform package, which per the spec's own SPEC DECISION at docs/01-spec.md:769 is *never* an independently-registered `Package` — it's an extra manifest belonging to some other, owning `Package`). Without this index populated, any `callisto.toml` naming a platform package's own npm name in a group's `members` list would fail hard with `GraphError::MissingGroupMember`, and `napi_drift` (in `crates/callisto-graph/src/napi.rs`) — which computes `member_triples` by reading `role_to_triple` off each group's `GroupMember::PlatformManifest` members — would never receive any real platform members to check against declared `napi.targets`.

## The fix (three coordinated changes)

1. **`identity.rs`**: `IdentityIndex.platform`'s value type changed from `(PackageId, PathBuf)` to `(PackageId, PathBuf, ManifestRole)` — the role is now carried in the index itself (computed once in walk.rs, where `detect_npm_role` already produced it) rather than needing a second/third disk read downstream. 123	impl<'a, R: CommandRunner, D: DependencyResolver> Workspace<'a, R, D> {
124	    /// Returns the workspace's [`TagIndex`], building it on first access and
125	    /// reusing the cached result afterwards. See the doc comment on the
126	    /// `tags` field for why this is deferred rather than built eagerly by
127	    /// [`Workspace::load`].
128	    pub fn tags(&self) -> Result<&TagIndex, GraphError> {
129	        if let Some(existing) = self.tags.get() {
130	            return Ok(existing);
131	        }
132	        let built = TagIndex::build(self.git_access(), &self.graph, &self.config)?;
133	        // `OnceCell::set` only fails if another write already raced it in;
134	        // `Workspace` is only ever accessed through `&self` here (never
135	        // shared across threads -- `R`/`D` carry no such bound), so the
136	        // `get()` check above already ruled that out. Fall back to `get()`
137	        // either way rather than trusting the `set` call's own return value,
138	        // so this stays correct even if that assumption ever changes.
139	        self.tags.set(built).ok();
140	        Ok(self
141	            .tags
142	            .get()
143	            .expect("tags was just set above, or already set by a prior call"))
144	    }
145	
146	    /// Returns the workspace's shared [`GitAccess`], discovering it on
147	    /// first access and reusing the cached result afterwards -- mirrors
148	    /// [`Workspace::tags`]. Every command that needs git (tag resolution,
149	    /// head SHA lookup, commit history walks, ...) should go through this
150	    /// rather than calling `GitAccess::discover` itself, so a single
151	    /// command invocation never pays for more than one discovery

153	    /// when gix is unavailable) regardless of how many of those it needs.

input.prompt:
You are reviewing an uncommitted change to `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/status.rs`. Run `git diff -- crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/status.rs` to see the exact change. Do not trust any summary from me — read the diff and current source yourself.

## Context

`Workspace` (in `crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`) has a lazily-built, cached `git: OnceCell<GitAccess<'a>>` field with a `git_access()` accessor (`self.git.get_or_init(|| GitAccess::discover(&self.root, self.runner))`), specifically built so that a single command invocation never pays for more than one `GitAccess::discover()` (a real gix-repository-open-or-CommandRunner-shell-fallback). `Workspace::tags()` already routes through `self.git_access()` internally (confirmed at `lib.rs:132`: `TagIndex::build(self.git_access(), &self.graph, &self.config)?`).

Before this change, `status()` in `commands/status.rs` called `ws.tags()?` (which populates the shared `git` cache as a side effect) and then, a few lines later, called `GitAccess::discover(&ws.root, ws.runner)` directly — constructing a completely separate, second `GitAccess` instance that bypasses the cache entirely. This is a real, if purely performance-related, redundancy: a second gix-repository-open attempt (or CommandRunner shell round-trip when gix is unavailable) for the exact same repository, in the same command invocation.

The fix: replaced `let git = GitAccess::discover(&ws.root, ws.runner);` with `let git = ws.git_access();`, removed the now-unused `use callisto_vcs::GitAccess;` import, and simplified `changed_since_last_tag(ws.runner, &ws.root, pkg, tags, &git)?` to `changed_since_last_tag(ws.runner, &ws.root, pkg, tags, git)?` (since `git` is now already a `&GitAccess<'_>` reference, not an owned value, so the old `&git` would have been a redundant double-reference that only compiled via deref coercion).

**No red/green test was written for this specific change**, on the documented reasoning that the fix has zero observable behavioral difference — `status()`'s output (the `StatusReport` it returns) is provably identical whether it uses a freshly-discovered `GitAccess` or the shared cached one, since both instances behave identically for the same repository and the same `CommandRunner`. The only difference is the elimination of one redundant discovery's I/O cost, which isn't observable through `status()`'s public API or return value. The existing 3 unit tests in `status.rs`'s own test module, plus the full `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib` suite (244 tests) and `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings`, were run and confirmed clean/passing after the change (you don't need to trust this — re-run them yourself per item 4 below).

## Your job

1. **Verify the "no observable behavioral difference" claim is actually true**, not just asserted. Read `GitAccess::discover`'s implementation (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/access.rs`) and confirm that two separately-constructed `GitAccess` instances against the same `root`/`runner` really would behave identically for every operation `status()`'s code path uses (`tags.last_tag`, `changed_since_last_tag`'s internal `GitDataSource` calls) — i.e. that there's no hidden state, caching, or side effect inside `GitAccess`/`GitRepository`/`ShellGit` construction or operation that could make the shared instance behave differently from a fresh one (e.g. some kind of internal memoization that a fresh instance wouldn't have yet, or a mutable side effect from discovery itself). If you find any such difference, that's a real finding — it would mean the "purely a performance fix" framing is wrong and this needs a real test.
2. **Verify no other call site in `status.rs` needed the same fix.** Confirm the diff removes the only `GitAccess::discover` call in the file (grep to be sure) and that nothing else in the file's git-related logic was missed.
3. **Verify the type change at the call site is correct**, not just that it compiles. `ws.git_access()` returns `&GitAccess<'a>`. Confirm `changed_since_last_tag`'s signature (`crates/callisto-graph/src/changed.rs`) really does expect `git: &GitAccess<'_>` (not an owned `GitAccess`), so passing `git` directly (rather than `&git`) is correct and not accidentally passing the wrong thing.
4. **Run the real checks yourself, don't trust that they were clean before**: `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib`, `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Also specifically re-run `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib commands::status` to see the 3 status-specific tests pass individually.
5. **Search for sibling gaps**: grep the whole `callisto-graph` crate for any other `GitAccess::discover(` call site that could/should be using `ws.git_access()` instead but doesn't (this consolidation was previously done for `plan_publish`/`aggregate`/`version`/`tags` in an earlier commit — check `git log --oneline -- crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs` if useful context — but is there anything else, beyond `status.rs`, that still calls `GitAccess::discover` directly instead of going through the shared accessor?). This crate's task backlog has a separate, not-yet-done item for `plan_snapshot` specifically — you don't need to fix that, just note if you find it (or anything else) during your search, so it's not missed.

Report every issue found as a concrete finding: file, line, what's wrong, and what the correct fix would be. If the "no behavioral difference" claim doesn't hold, explain exactly why and what test would be needed. If everything checks out, say so explicitly and state what you verified for each of the 5 items. Keep the report under 500 words unless a real issue needs detail.

content.text:
All 5 verification items checked directly against source. Findings below.

## Summary: change is correct; no behavioral difference; no urgent gaps in status.rs itself

**1. "No observable behavioral difference" — confirmed true.**
`GitAccess::discover` (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/access.rs:51-57`) is pure construction: `GitRepository::discover(root).ok()` (which just calls `gix::discover` — no caching, `gix::Repository` is a fresh handle) plus `ShellGit::new(runner, root.to_path_buf())` (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs:52-58`, just stores `&dyn CommandRunner` + a `PathBuf`, no internal state). Every `GitDataSource` method on `GitAccess` (`access.rs:60-128`) is a pure read/dispatch with no mutation of `self` and no memoization field anywhere in `GitAccess`, `GitRepository`, or `ShellGit`. Two independently-constructed instances against the same `root`/`runner` are behaviorally indistinguishable for every operation `status()`'s path uses (`tags.last_tag` is a `TagIndex` lookup, not a `GitAccess` call at all; `changed_since_last_tag` only calls `git.commits_since`). The claim holds — this really is a pure I/O-cost fix with no test needed.

**2. Only `GitAccess::discover` call site in the file — confirmed.** Grep of `status.rs` shows the diff removed the file's only occurrence; nothing else in the file touches git directly.

**3. Type change is correct.** `changed_since_last_tag` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/changed.rs:23-29`) takes `git: &GitAccess<'_>`. `Workspace::git_access()` (`lib.rs:154-157`) returns `&GitAccess<'a>`. Passing `git` (not `&git`) at the call site is exactly right — the old code's `&git` was a redundant `&&GitAccess` only accepted via deref coercion.

**4. Checks re-run, all clean.**
- `cargo build --workspace` — clean.
- `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib` — 244 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib commands::status` — 3/3 pass individually.

**5. Sibling gaps found (2, both pre-existing, not introduced by this diff):**
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/snapshot.rs:20` — `plan_snapshot` still calls `callisto_vcs::GitAccess::discover(&ws.root, ws.runner).head_sha()` directly instead of `ws.git_access()`. This matches the already-tracked backlog item #33 ("Route plan_snapshot through ws.git_access()") — not a new finding, just confirmed present.
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/infer.rs:77` — `CommitInference::infer` (behind `feature = "inference"`) calls `GitAccess::discover(&self.root, self.runner)` fresh. This is a **new** gap not on the tracked backlog: `aggregate()` calls `inference.infer(pkg, window)` once per package in a `for pkg in graph.packages()` loop (`aggregate.rs:187,223`), so if `CommitInference` were ever wired up in production it would reproduce the exact N-discoveries-per-workspace bug that `status()`/`changed_since_last_tag` were fixed for. Currently this is dead in practice — grep confirms `CommitInference` is never constructed anywhere in the workspace (`callisto-cli` always passes `NoInference`; no test constructs it either) — so it's latent, not live, but worth flagging since `CommitInference` doesn't hold a `Workspace` reference (only `runner`/`root`), so fixing it would require either threading a `&GitAccess` through `SeverityInference::infer` or giving `CommitInference` its own `OnceCell`.

Other `GitAccess::discover(` occurrences (`tags.rs:89` inside `last_tag_for`, all `aggregate.rs`/`changed.rs` occurrences beyond what's listed) are confirmed to be either test-only (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests`) or, for `last_tag_for`, a standalone documented-as-such API with no production caller (only exercised by its own test module) — not sibling gaps.

No blocking issues. The status.rs change is correct as described.

## 14. Config format

Hybrid: workspace-level `callisto.toml` for cross-package concerns, per-project `moon.yml`
extension block for package-scoped overrides.

```toml
# callisto.toml
[changesets]
dir = ".changeset"

[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"   # out-of-range | always — §7.4's cascade-trigger axis: WHEN to
                         # cascade a dependent at all (default: only when its declared spec
                         # no longer covers the new version)
bump-severity = "patch"   # patch | minor — §7.4's cascade-severity axis: HOW HARD to bump a
                           # dependent once cascade fires (a distinct axis from `mode` above;
                           # earlier drafts conflated these into one four-value key)
peer-escalation = true   # peer-dep out-of-range non-patch escalates to major (§13 inv. 9);
                          # true by default, opt-out not opt-in — set false to disable
preserve-npm-ranges = true   # §7.3/§13 inv. 15 — if a bump can't be confidently
                              # round-tripped, leave the original range string untouched and
                              # warn rather than overwriting it; this key gates whether
                              # range-preserving rewrite is attempted at all (true is the
                              # only sane default — false would mean always overwriting to
                              # an exact version, knope-style, which this design rejects)

[validation]
allow-empty-changesets = false   # §6.3 — misfiled under [cascade] in earlier drafts; this is
                                  # a validation setting, not a cascade one

[[package-set]]
match = "crates/*"
release-trigger = "auto"
publish-to = ["cratesIo"]
pre-major-inference = "conservative"   # §7.1 — opt-in remap of inferred (not explicit)
                                        # severities for Auto-trigger packages at 0.y.z,
                                        # y > 0; omit/false to leave inference unremapped.
                                        # Available on [[package-set]]/[[package]]/
                                        # [[fixed-group]]/[[linked-group]] blocks alike —
                                        # shown here since Rust/0.x crates are the case P1's
```

```yaml
# packages/foo/moon.yml
extensions:
  callisto:
    package-name: foo
    release-trigger: changeset
    publish-to: [cratesIo, npm]
    tag-template: "foo@{version}"
```

Discovery walks the workspace (moon's project graph when available for authoritative
project roots, `ignore`-crate walk otherwise — `ProjectLocator`, §0.1/§15); `package-set`
matches expand to concrete packages; explicit `[[package]]` entries always win over set
matches. A set matching nothing, or two sets claiming the same package, is a hard config
error. **Group membership validation, at parse time (P5), not at mutation time**: a package
must belong to at most one `[[fixed-group]]` and at most one `[[linked-group]]`, and the
fixed and linked member sets must be disjoint — reject with a clear error listing the
conflicting groups, rather than letting an ambiguous membership surface as a confusing
mutation-time alignment failure.

**Path-like values (`[changesets].dir`, `[[package]]`/`[[package-set]] changelog`) always use
forward slashes (`/`), never backslashes, regardless of the OS the value was authored or is
read on.** `callisto.toml` is checked into version control and read by developers and CI on
whatever platform they're on; the parsed value goes through the same `workspace_relative`
normalization used for real filesystem-discovered paths (§M.1.3), which only *converts* a
native separator to `/` on the platform that's actually running — on POSIX, `\` is a legal
filename character, not a separator, so a Windows-authored `dir = "custom\\subdir"` value
would be read back as one oddly-named directory (`custom\subdir`, one component) rather than
two nested ones the moment the same file is read on macOS or Linux CI. Writing `dir =
"custom/subdir"` is portable on every platform this tool runs on, including Windows.

input.subject: Fix index.native's Case D key mismatch for platform package dependency edges
input.description:
Discovered during the IdentityIndex.platform wiring fix's review (independent review agent, out-of-scope for that task, not a defect in that diff).

In crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs's identity-building loop, index.native.insert((*eco, primary_id.name().to_string()), primary_id.clone()) keys the native (ecosystem, name) -> PackageId index on primary_id.name() for every ecosystem entry in list, rather than that specific entry's own id.name().

In a Case D directory (a Cargo.toml and a differently-named package.json sharing one directory — the same scenario already fixed for index.platform), this means the npm-ecosystem manifest's own name (e.g. a platform package like @myorg/my-crate-linux-x64-gnu) never gets a native index entry under its own name — only under the Cargo-derived primary_id's name. If some OTHER npm manifest declares a dependency (e.g. optionalDependencies) on that platform package by its literal own npm name, index.native.get((Ecosystem::Npm, "@myorg/my-crate-linux-x64-gnu")) would return None and the dependency edge would silently fail to resolve, with no diagnostic.

Likely fix (needs verification): use id.name() (the per-ecosystem entry's own resolved identity) instead of primary_id.name() when inserting into index.native, mirroring the index.platform fix's exact reasoning. Needs its own red test proving a real optionalDependencies edge onto a Case D platform package currently fails to resolve, then the fix, then verification it resolves correctly — full TDD rigor.

input.subject: Fix CommitInference::infer's per-package GitAccess::discover redundancy (currently latent/unwired)
input.description:
Discovered during the status.rs GitAccess-consolidation fix's review (independent review agent, out-of-scope for that task).

crates/callisto-graph/src/infer.rs, inside CommitInference::infer (behind the "inference" feature), calls callisto_vcs::GitAccess::discover(&self.root, self.runner) fresh on every call. aggregate() calls inference.infer(pkg, window) once per package in a loop, so if CommitInference were ever actually constructed in production, this would reproduce the exact N-discoveries-per-workspace redundancy already fixed for status()/plan_publish/tags.

Currently latent, not live: confirmed via grep that CommitInference is never constructed anywhere in the workspace today — callisto-cli always passes NoInference, and no test constructs it either. Dead code in practice, not a live bug, but would become one the moment commit-severity inference is wired up to a real caller.

Fix would require either threading a &GitAccess through SeverityInference::infer's signature (a trait method — check NoInference too, since this is a real API change with wider blast radius), or giving CommitInference its own lazily-built OnceCell<GitAccess> field mirroring Workspace's pattern. Needs investigation into how "inference" feature callers are expected to construct/reuse CommitInference before choosing an approach — full TDD rigor once scoped.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Error Taxonomy — Semantic Model

Source: `crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs`

## GraphError Variants

### With E-codes (user-facing, miette Diagnostic)

| Code | Variant | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| E100 | `DuplicatePackage { id, paths }` | Same PackageId discovered at two different workspace paths |
| E101 | `SplitIdentity { path, ids }` | A single manifest path declares two conflicting PackageIds |
| E102 | `UnknownPackage { id }` | A PackageId referenced in config or a plan is not in the workspace |
| E103 | `AmbiguousName { name, candidates }` | A bare name matches packages in 2+ ecosystems; caller must use prefixed form |
| E104 | `Cycle { cycle }` | Dependency cycle detected in the workspace graph |
| E105 | `CascadeNotConverged { iterations }` | Cascade failed to reach a fixed point |
| E106 | `FixedGroupDivergent { group, members }` | Fixed group members have different on-disk versions |
| E107 | `GroupGrammarMismatch { group, members }` | Fixed group members use incompatible versioning grammars |
| E108 | `MissingGroupMember { group, member }` | A group lists a member that is not in the workspace |
| E109 | `ConflictingGroupMembership { package, groups }` | A package is listed in two or more groups |
| E114 | `PreJson(PreJsonError)` | Failed to parse .changeset/pre.json |
| E115 | `PreJsonRead { message }` | Failed to read .changeset/pre.json |
| E116 (ConfigError) | `InvalidChangesetsDir { dir }` | changesets.dir contains `..` path components |
| E117 | `UnexpectedManifestVersion { path, expected_from, expected_to, found }` | Manifest version is neither bump.from nor bump.to; requires human intervention |

### Without E-codes (transparent or internal)

| Variant | Source / Notes |
|---|---|
| `Locate(LocateError)` | Transparent from locate module |
| `Manifest(ManifestError)` | Transparent from callisto-manifests |
| `Config(ConfigError)` | Transparent; see ConfigError section below |
| `Format(ParseError)` | Transparent from callisto-format |
| `ParseChangeset { path, source }` | Changeset file parse failure (not transparent — adds path context) |
| `Bump(BumpError)` | Transparent from callisto-format |
| `Changelog(ChangelogError)` | Transparent from callisto-changelog |
| `Conventional(ConventionalError)` | Feature-gated; transparent |
| `TagTemplate(TagTemplateError)` | Not transparent |
| `VersionParse(VersionParseError)` | Not transparent |
| `Model(ModelError)` | Transparent from callisto-model |
| `Vcs(VcsError)` | Transparent from callisto-vcs |
| `Command(CommandError)` | Not transparent; wraps git/fs failures |
| `OnDiskVersionDrift { package, expected, found }` | On-disk version changed since plan was generated |
| `WorkspaceVersionConflict { root_manifest, details }` | Workspace root has conflicting version updates |
| `GrammarMismatch { from, to, source }` | Incompatible versioning grammars on a dependency edge |

## ConfigError Variants

ConfigError is always wrapped in `GraphError::Config` (transparent). All ConfigError variants
surface to the user as GraphError.

### With E-codes

| Code | Variant | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| E110 | `Read { path, message }` | Failed to read callisto.toml or moon.yml |
| E111 | `ParseToml { path, message }` | Invalid TOML syntax in callisto.toml |
| E116 | `InvalidChangesetsDir { dir }` | changesets.dir escapes workspace root |

### Without E-codes

| Variant | Status | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `PackageMatchedNothing { pattern }` | Defined but NEVER EMITTED — known gap | A [[package]] rule matched no packages after workspace walk |
| `PackageSetMatchedNothing { pattern }` | Defined but NEVER EMITTED — known gap | A [[package-set]] rule matched no packages |
| `OverlappingPackageSets { package, patterns }` | Defined but NEVER EMITTED — known gap | A package is claimed by two [[package-set]] rules |
| `ConflictingGroupNames { group, other, member }` | Active | Same member in two groups |
| `EmptyGroup { group }` | Active | A group has no members |
| `DuplicateGroupName { group }` | Active | Two groups with the same name |
| `UnknownRegistry { key }` | Active | publish-to references a registry key not in [registries.*] |
| `UnknownKey { path, key }` | Active | serde deny_unknown_fields rejection |
| `InvalidBumpSeverity { found }` | Active | cascade.bump-severity is not "patch" or "minor" |
| `InvalidPreMajorInference { found }` | Active | pre-major-inference is not a valid value |
| `Tag(TagTemplateError)` | Active | Invalid tag template syntax |
| `VersionParse(VersionParseError)` | Active | Invalid version string in config |

## Conventions

- Use `GraphError::Command(CommandError::Io { ... })` for filesystem I/O errors that aren't
  manifest parse failures.
- `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` variants inherit the inner type's miette diagnostic code.
  Do NOT add `code()` to a transparent variant.
- `#[allow(clippy::result_large_err)]` is set at the enum level — do not add it per-variant.
- New variants go at the bottom of the enum unless they belong to an existing logical group.
- `#[non_exhaustive]` is on both enums — external crates cannot exhaustively match them.

1. `E020`: `callisto-model/src/exec.rs` (`CommandError` variant) vs `callisto-model/src/version.rs` (`VersionParseError`)
2. `E021`: `callisto-model/src/exec.rs` vs `callisto-model/src/version.rs` (`GrammarMismatch`)
3. `E025`: `callisto-model/src/exec.rs` vs `callisto-model/src/commit.rs` (`CommitWalkError::RefNotFound`)

6. `E052`: `callisto-format/src/changeset/mod.rs` (`WriteError::EmptyName`) vs `callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs` (`VcsError::RefNotFound`)

- `commit.rs`: `CommitWalkError::RefNotFound` E025→E054 (same reasoning)
- `changeset/mod.rs`: `ParseError::EmptySummary` E048→E055 (kept `EmptyChangeset`'s E048, since it's declared first in the enum)
- `changeset/mod.rs`: `WriteError::EmptySummary` E050→E056, `WriteError::EmptyName` E052→E057 (kept `callisto-vcs`'s E050-E053 block untouched — it's a clean, fully-contiguous 4-code run already documented in `docs/01-spec.md`'s §V.2 as "chosen not to collide with callisto-model's or callisto-graph's ranges", a claim that was actually false before this fix and becomes true after it)
- `error.rs`: `ConfigError::InvalidChangelogPath` E117→E113 (kept `GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion`'s E117, since it's the one documented in `.claude/semantic-model/error-taxonomy.md`)

Check for any place in the whole workspace (not just docs) that pattern-matches or asserts on the OLD code value as a string literal (e.g. a test doing `assert!(matches!(err.code()...))` is fine since miette's `code()` returns a `Box<dyn Display>` typically compared via string formatting in tests, or a test literally checking `"E020"` etc.) — grep for the 7 old code strings (`"E020"`, `"E021"`, `"E025"`, `"E048"`, `"E050"`, `"E052"`, `"E117"`) across all test files, not just the ones already touched, to catch any test elsewhere in the workspace that might assert on one of the OLD values tied to the specific variant that moved (as opposed to the code that correctly stayed put, which coincidentally still has the same string).
3. **Verify the new `extract_diagnostic_codes` scanner is actually correct against the real files**, not just the synthetic test fixtures. In particular check: does it correctly handle a `code(E117)` split across multiple lines with different indentation (several real variants in the diff format it as `\n        code(E117),\n` — multi-line, not single-line)? 4. **Verify the `include_str!` relative paths are all correct** by checking each resolves to the file the display-name string claims (an easy copy-paste mistake to make with 10 parallel paths) — cross-reference each `include_str!(...)` path against the tuple's own display-name string.
5. **Verify the choice of which side to renumber in each collision was reasonable** (not necessarily the only correct choice, but not arbitrary/wrong either) — spot check at least 2 of the 7: does `callisto-vcs`'s E050-E053 block really appear contiguous and undisturbed, and does `docs/01-spec.md`'s §V.2 (search for "chosen not to collide") really make the claim described above, and is it actually true now?
6. **Run the real checks yourself, don't trust that they were clean before**: `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test -p callisto-model -p callisto-format -p callisto-graph --lib`, `cargo clippy -p callisto-model -p callisto-format -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and specifically `cargo test -p callisto-model --lib diagnostic_code` to see the 3 new/rewritten tests individually.
7. **Search for a sibling gap**: is there any diagnostic-code-bearing file in the workspace NOT in the 10-file `DIAGNOSTIC_CODE_SOURCE_FILES` list? Do a fresh `grep -rl "code(E[0-9]" crates/*/src/**/*.rs crates/*/src/*.rs` and diff it against the 10 files list yourself — don't just trust the list is complete.

Report every issue found as a concrete finding: file, line, what's wrong, and the correct fix. This is a correctness-critical fix touching user-facing error codes across 5 crates plus a load-bearing regression test — if you find anything wrong, however minor, report it in detail. fix(model,format,graph): resolve 7 duplicate diagnostic codes, replace broken uniqueness test

Started as a single known collision (GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion
and ConfigError::InvalidChangelogPath both claiming E117), but a full
workspace scan for every code(E..) occurrence surfaced six more real,
previously-undetected duplicates:

- E020: exec.rs's CommandError vs version.rs's VersionParseError
- E021: exec.rs's CommandError vs version.rs's GrammarMismatch
- E025: exec.rs's CommandError vs commit.rs's CommitWalkError::RefNotFound
- E048: changeset/mod.rs's ParseError::EmptyChangeset vs its own
  ParseError::EmptySummary (same enum, same file)
- E050: changeset/mod.rs's WriteError::EmptySummary vs callisto-vcs's
  VcsError::RepoNotFound
- E052: changeset/mod.rs's WriteError::EmptyName vs callisto-vcs's
  VcsError::RefNotFound

Each collision was resolved by renumbering the side that wasn't part of
an already-clean, contiguous, or already-documented block, into a free
slot the same scan identified (E029, E034, E054-E057, E113) -- no
#[error(...)] message, field, or help() text changed, only the E-code.

The root cause these all shared: test_all_diagnostic_codes_are_unique
(callisto-model/src/lib.rs) was supposed to catch exactly this class of
bug but used a hand-maintained &[&str] list that had drifted badly out
of sync -- missing two entire files (commit.rs, version.rs) and roughly
a third of callisto-graph/src/error.rs's own codes, so E117 wasn't even
in the list it was meant to check. Replaced it with a scan that embeds
every diagnostic-code-bearing file's real source text at compile time
via include_str! and extracts every code(E<digits>) occurrence directly,
so a new code anywhere in those files is covered automatically with no
list to remember to update.

Independent review (re-deriving the full collision set from scratch,
re-running every check fresh, and a live mutation test reverting one
renumbering to confirm the test still fails for the right reason) found
one real gap: three doc comments in config/raw.rs still cited the old
E117 for InvalidChangelogPath after the E113 renumbering -- fixed here.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HxMVynBHufrDkmRHgmKgcH
EOF

    #[error("failed to read `{path}`: {message}")]

    #[error("[[package-set]] `{pattern}` matched no packages")]
    PackageSetMatchedNothing { pattern: String },

    #[error("[[package]] `{pattern}` matched no package")]
    PackageMatchedNothing { pattern: String },

    /// §14: "two sets claiming the same package is a hard config error."
    #[error("package `{package}` is claimed by more than one [[package-set]]: {}",
