# Autonomous loop check

You're being invoked on a timer while the user is away or occupied. The point is to keep work moving forward without the user driving every step — finishing things they started, maintaining PRs they're building, catching problems before they come back to find them. You're a steward, not an initiator. The user set you loose on their work, and the value you provide comes from reliably advancing things they've already set in motion, not from finding new things to do.

The key tension to navigate: the user trusts you enough to run autonomously, but that trust is easily lost. Acting on what the conversation already established is safe and valuable. Inventing new work or making irreversible changes without clear authorization erodes trust fast. When you're unsure whether something falls into "continuing established work" or "inventing new work," lean toward the former only when the transcript provides clear evidence the user wanted it done. If you find yourself reaching for justifications about why a push is probably fine, that's a signal to wait.

## What to act on

The current conversation is your highest-signal source — re-read the transcript above, since everything there is something the user was actively engaged with. The strongest signal is an in-progress PR you've been building together: review comments to address and resolve, failing CI checks to diagnose (and re-enqueue if they're flakes), merge conflicts to fix. The goal is to get the PR into a state where it's ready to merge pending only human review — the user shouldn't come back to find a PR blocked on things you could have handled. After that, look for unfinished implementation where the last exchange left something half-done, and explicit "I'll also..." or "next I'll..." commitments the conversation made and didn't honor. Weaker but still real: dangling questions you could now answer, verification steps that were skipped, edge cases that were mentioned but not handled, and natural continuations that don't require new decisions.

If you find anything in this category, act on it — actually do the work, don't describe what could be done. Run the tests, don't say "you could run the tests." The whole point of autonomous operation is that work gets done while the user is away.

When the conversation transcript has nothing left, the current branch's pull/merge request on the user's SCM is the next-best place to look. This is maintenance work — valuable, but lower priority than continuing the user's active work. Find the PR/MR for the current branch via the SCM's CLI, then check three things: CI status, unresolved review threads, and whether the branch has fallen behind the base. For failing CI, pull the failing job's logs and diagnose before acting — flaky-shaped failures (timeout, runner died, transient network) can be re-enqueued; real failures need a reproduction and a minimal fix. For unresolved review threads, fetch the comment, address the feedback, push, and resolve the thread via, for example, the GitHub GraphQL `resolveReviewThread` mutation (or the equivalent for whichever SCM the project uses). Before pushing anything, check whether someone else has pushed to the branch while you were working — if so, rebase (don't merge) to keep history clean.

When CI is green, threads are clear, and there's idle time, sweeping the branch for issues is a good use of that time — bug-hunt or simplification passes catch problems before reviewers do, saving everyone a round-trip.

If everything is genuinely quiet — no conversation work, no PR maintenance — say so in one sentence and stop. No summary of what you checked, no list of what you might do later. The user will see your message in the transcript when they come back; three consecutive "nothing to do" results means you should scale back to a quick CI check and stop, not narrate.

## Repeated invocations

If you see earlier autonomous checks in this conversation, adjust your scope accordingly. If a previous check left a question the user hasn't answered, the cost of acting depends on reversibility: for reversible actions (local edits, running tests), make your best call and proceed; for irreversible ones (pushing, deleting, sending), keep waiting — the cost of acting wrongly on something irreversible is much higher than the cost of waiting one more cycle. If three or more consecutive checks have found nothing actionable, things are quiet — do one quick CI/threads check and stop in a single line. Repeated "nothing to do" messages clutter the transcript and waste the user's attention when they come back to review.

Read and analyze freely — understanding the state of things has no blast radius. Make edits and run tests when you're confident they continue established work. Commit and push only when you're clearly continuing something the user authorized, or when the work pattern makes the intent obvious — like fixing CI on a PR you've been building together.


---

# Autonomous loop tick (dynamic pacing)

Run the autonomous check using the loop instructions established earlier in this conversation. If you cannot find them, treat this as a no-op tick.

You scheduled this tick via the ScheduleWakeup tool (not a recurring cron). To keep the loop alive, call ScheduleWakeup again at the end of this turn with `prompt` set to the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` — otherwise the loop ends after this tick.

If a Monitor is armed (check TaskList), keep `delaySeconds` at 1200–1800s — the Monitor is the wake signal and this is only the fallback heartbeat. If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`, handle the event before deciding whether to re-arm. To stop the loop, call ScheduleWakeup with `stop: true` and TaskStop the monitor (use TaskList to find its task ID if no longer in context).

Use PushNotification when the loop can't move further without the user, or when something landed that they'd want to act on now: newly blocked on a decision you won't make alone, third straight tick with nothing to do, you're ending the loop, or a major update arrived (CI went red, a review changes the plan). Progress you made yourself isn't a trigger — the transcript covers that. One ping per state, not per tick.

6692	
6693	#### G.6.3 Release triggers and the pre-major remap
6694	
6695	`ReleaseTrigger::Changeset` packages take their severity from changesets only.
6696	`ReleaseTrigger::Auto` packages take theirs from changesets when a changeset names them, and
6697	from inference otherwise — §7.1's "a changeset always wins over inference," enforced here
6698	rather than inside `callisto-conventional` (§C.7).
6699	
6700	§7.1's opt-in pre-major remap is applied to the inferred severity, on this side of the seam:
6701	
6702	```rust
6703	/// §7.1 / the decision doc's 0.x-remap resolution, stated as a function so the rule has one
6704	/// written form. Applied **only** to an inferred severity for an `Auto`-trigger package, never
6705	/// to a changeset severity, and never inside `bump_version` (§6.2 stays rigid — no flag, no
6706	/// config path reaches it, ever).
6707	///
6708	/// This crate — not `callisto-conventional` — owns the policy value: it reads it from config
6709	/// (§G.5.3), hands it across the seam in `InferenceWindowSpec::policy`, and is the sole
6710	/// production caller, inside `CommitInference::infer()` (§G.6.4), right after
6711	/// `callisto_conventional::infer_severity` (§C.7) returns a **raw**, unremapped severity.
6712	/// `callisto-conventional` deliberately does not apply this policy itself — bump-decision
6713	/// policy is coordination logic (P6), which belongs here, not in the commit-classification
6714	/// crate. `NoInference` never calls this function at all: it returns `Ok(None)` before any
6715	/// severity exists to remap, so the only other caller is `callisto-fixtures`' direct unit
6716	/// tests of this function as a pure transform.
6717	///
6718	/// Returns `(severity, remapped)`; `remapped` populates `BumpReason::Inference.remapped`,
6719	/// which is what lets §18 Q5.4's attribution line say the remap fired.
6720	pub fn apply_pre_major(
6721	    inferred: Severity,
6722	    policy: PreMajorInferencePolicy,
6723	    current: &Version,
6724	    has_prior_release: bool,
6725	) -> (Severity, bool);
6726	```
6727	
6728	```
6729	if policy is fully off                        → (inferred, false)
6730	if current is not `0.y.z`                     → (inferred, false)
6731	if current is `0.0.z`                         → (inferred, false)   # inert, and says so
6732	if the package has no prior release tag       → (inferred, false)   # inert, and says so
6733	
6734	match (policy, inferred):
6735	    (breaking_to_minor, Major) → (Minor, true)
6736	    (feat_to_patch,     Minor) → (Patch, true)
6737	    (_,                 s    ) → (s, false)
6738	```
6739	
6740	The two inert cases are the whole reason this is specified rather than inlined: `0.0.z` and
6741	no-prior-tag are exactly where release-please's `bumpMinorPreMajor` has leaked bugs for years
6742	(its `#2087` and `#2635`), and P2's stateless detection makes "no tag yet" a *routine* state
6743	rather than an edge case. When either fires and the policy is not off, `apply_pre_major` also
6744	emits a `Diagnostic` naming `ConfigKey::PRE_MAJOR_INFERENCE` and saying the setting is inert for
6745	this package and why. The code is `DiagnosticCode::PreMajorInferenceInert` (§M.11.2), severity
6746	`Warning`, `governed_by: Some(ConfigKey::PRE_MAJOR_INFERENCE)`, no `escalated_by` — this is
6747	§7.1's "no remap, tool says so explicitly," and §13 invariant 28's attribution rule applied to
6748	a default that *didn't* fire, so there is no strictness level at which it should become a
6749	failure.
6750	
6751	> `[SPEC DECISION, not in 00-design.md: `apply_pre_major` is applied to the already-aggregated
6752	> (max-of-all-commits) severity `callisto_conventional::infer_severity` (§C.7) returns, not
6753	> per-commit before aggregation.]` §7.1's phrasing ("applied only when producing a severity
6754	> for an `Auto`-trigger package") describes singular output, consistent with either order, so
6755	> this is a genuine choice. The two orders are provably equivalent for this policy's specific
6756	> transform table (`Major → Minor`, `Minor → Patch`, both monotonic and each keyed to a
6757	> severity value that can only originate from one commit-type family — `Severity::Minor` can
6758	> only come from a `feat` commit, `Severity::Major` only from a breaking one), so equivalence
6759	> is not an assumption, it is a consequence of the transform table having no case where two
6760	> different raw severities could collide into the same post-remap value from different
6761	> sources. Aggregate-then-remap is simpler (one call site, not N) and makes `remapped`'s
6762	> "changed the *inferred* severity" semantics a direct equality check on the aggregate rather
6763	> than something reconstructed from per-commit deltas.
6764	
6765	> `[SPEC DECISION, not in 00-design.md: the pre-major gate reads `Version::major()`/`minor()`
6766	> and therefore only makes sense for `VersionGrammar::SemVer`.]` §7.1's "`0.y.z`" language is
6767	> SemVer notation and both v0.1–v0.4's committed ecosystems (Cargo, npm) are SemVer-grammar
6768	> (§7.7), so this is not a live gap today, but §M.4.1's `Version` is grammar-tagged precisely
6769	> because a future ecosystem might not be. `apply_pre_major` is specified to be called only
6770	> for SemVer-grammar `Version`s; a caller invoking it for a non-SemVer version is a caller
6771	> bug, not something this function defends against by returning an `Err` — adding a fallible
6772	> signature to every call site for a case that cannot occur under any committed milestone is
6773	> the kind of speculative generality P4 warns against paying for before an ecosystem that
6774	> needs it exists.
6775	
6776	#### G.6.4 `SeverityInference` — the seam
6777	
6778	```rust
6779	/// The seam between aggregation and conventional-commit inference. Owned by this crate, not
6780	/// by `callisto-conventional`, so that v0.1 can ship a working `version` with no inference
6781	/// crate in the dependency tree at all (§17).
6782	pub trait SeverityInference {
6783	    /// `Ok(None)` means "this package has no inferred severity" — the routine answer at v0.1
6784	    /// and for any `ReleaseTrigger::Changeset` package.
6785	    fn infer(&self, pkg: &Package, window: InferenceWindowSpec<'_>)
6786	        -> Result<Option<InferenceOutcome>, GraphError>;
6787	}
6788	
6789	/// What the caller knows and the impl needs: pathspecs, the lower bound, and the pre-major
6790	/// gate's two inputs. Mirrors `callisto-conventional`'s `InferenceInput` (§C.7) without this
6791	/// crate's default build having to name that crate's types.
6792	pub struct InferenceWindowSpec<'a> {
6793	    pub pathspecs: &'a [PathBuf],
6794	    pub since: Option<CommitSha>,
6795	    pub current_version: &'a Version,
6796	    pub has_prior_release: bool,
6797	    pub policy: PreMajorInferencePolicy,
6798	}
6799	
6800	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
6801	pub struct InferenceOutcome {
6802	    pub severity: Severity,
6803	    pub commit_count: usize,
6804	    pub remapped: bool,
6805	    /// `(sha, subject)` per commit, for `callisto-changelog`'s `ChangeSource::Commit`
6806	    /// itemisation (§CL.3). Empty for `NoInference`.
6807	    pub commits: Vec<(CommitSha, String)>,
6808	}
6809	
6810	/// v0.1's impl. Always `Ok(None)`. Not a placeholder to be deleted — it stays as the impl a
6811	/// caller selects when `inference` is off, and as the one `callisto-fixtures` uses for
6812	/// cascade tests that have no business running `git`.
6813	pub struct NoInference;
6814	
6815	/// v0.2's impl, behind the `inference` feature. A thin adapter over
6816	/// `callisto_conventional::infer_severity` (§C.7) — it holds a `&dyn CommandRunner` and the
6817	/// workspace root, translates `InferenceWindowSpec` into `InferenceInput`, and translates the
6818	/// result back.
6819	#[cfg(feature = "inference")]
6820	pub struct CommitInference<'a> { /* runner, root */ }
6821	
6822	impl<'a> SeverityInference for CommitInference<'a> {
6823	    fn infer(&self, pkg: &Package, window: InferenceWindowSpec<'_>)
6824	        -> Result<Option<InferenceOutcome>, GraphError>
6825	    {
6826	        let raw = callisto_conventional::infer_severity(self.runner, &self.root, &input)?;
6827	        if raw.commit_count == 0 { return Ok(None); }
6828	        let (severity, remapped) =
6829	            apply_pre_major(raw.severity, window.policy, window.current_version,
6830	                             window.has_prior_release);   // §G.6.3 — the ONE call site
6831	        Ok(Some(InferenceOutcome { severity, commit_count: raw.commit_count,
6832	                                    remapped, commits: raw.commits }))
6833	    }
6834	}
6835	```
6836	
6837	`callisto_conventional::infer_severity` (§C.7) returns a **raw**, unremapped severity — the
6838	pre-major policy is deliberately not applied inside `callisto-conventional` at all, even
6839	though an earlier draft of that crate's spec did so via a since-removed
6840	`apply_pre_major_policy` function (§C.4). Applying policy to a bump decision is coordination
6841	logic, and P6 puts coordination logic in `callisto-graph`, not in a crate whose job is commit
6842	*classification*; duplicating the transform in both crates (which that earlier draft did,
6843	verbatim) is the two-code-paths-for-one-concept shape invariant 25 warns against, just for
6844	this policy instead of tag identity. `NoInference` never reaches `apply_pre_major` at all —
6845	it returns `Ok(None)` unconditionally, before any severity exists to remap — so the function
6846	has exactly one production call site (above) plus `callisto-fixtures`' direct unit tests of
6847	it as a pure function; an earlier justification citing "the `NoInference` … path" for its
6848	existence was describing a call that doesn't happen and has been corrected (§G.6.3).
6849	
6850	> `[SPEC DECISION, not in 00-design.md: `SeverityInference` is a `callisto-graph`-owned seam,
6851	> and the concrete `callisto-conventional` adapter (`CommitInference`) lives **in
6852	> `callisto-graph`** behind an optional `inference` feature rather than in the wrappers.]`
6853	> §17 defers inference to v0.2, so v0.1 must be able to build and ship `version` without
6854	> `callisto-conventional`; a seam is the standard way to express that. The adapter's placement
6855	> is the reconciliation of two drafts that disagreed: one said `callisto-graph` must not depend
6856	> on `callisto-conventional` at all, the other had `callisto-cli` constructing a
6857	> `callisto_conventional::CommitInference` that implements a `callisto-graph` trait — which no
6858	> crate could actually write, since neither `callisto-conventional` (no graph dependency) nor
6859	> `callisto-cli` (which would then be the only place the adapter exists, forcing
6860	> `callisto-moon` to duplicate it) is a good home. An optional feature on `callisto-graph`
6861	> keeps the v0.1 dependency tree clean, keeps both wrappers thin (§13 inv. 27, P6), and keeps
6862	> exactly one adapter. §11 records it.
6863	
6864	#### G.6.5 The fixed-group severity union pre-step (§7.1)
6865	
6866	Before the cascade fixpoint runs, any severity assigned by changeset or inference to *any*
6867	member of a fixed group is unioned by max across every `GroupMember::Package` in that group.
6868	§7.1 is explicit that this is a single pre-step, not something interleaved with the fixpoint.
6869	§G.7.5 records the one place that claim needed strengthening.

Since `infer()` is called once per package inside `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs`'s `aggregate()` function loop (`for pkg in graph.packages() { ... inference.infer(pkg, window) ... }`), this meant an N-package workspace paid for N redundant git-repository discoveries — and `aggregate()` itself ALREADY receives a `git: &GitAccess<'_>` parameter from ITS OWN caller (a `Workspace`-shared, already-discovered instance — see the doc comment right above the `for pkg in graph.packages()` loop in aggregate.rs, which explains `git` is deliberately shared rather than discovered fresh, mirroring already-shipped sibling fixes for `plan_publish`/`status`/`plan_snapshot` in this same crate's git history). `CommitInference` never actually reused that already-available `git` — it ignored it and discovered its own.

input.description: While fixing docs/01-spec.md's WorkspaceVersionConflict field mismatch (task #7), discovered that crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs's PlannedBump-building loop (~line 116-121) only ever pushes VersionWriteTarget::Manifest(decl.path.clone()) for each Canonical-role manifest -- it never constructs VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage. Grepping the whole callisto-graph crate confirms VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage/DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency are never constructed anywhere in production (only apply.rs's own #[cfg(test)] fixtures build them via struct literal). This means: (1) apply.rs's classify_manifest_writes de-dup-by-root logic, its CargoWorkspacePackage/CargoWorkspaceDependency write handling, and GraphError::WorkspaceVersionConflict are all currently unreachable dead code in production; (2) more importantly, a real Cargo crate with `version.workspace = true` (inheriting its version from `[workspace.package].version` at the workspace root) may not get its version bumped correctly at all today, since the planner only ever targets each package's own Canonical manifest path directly -- writing `[package].version` on a manifest that doesn't have that key (because it inherits) would either no-op or write a field Cargo ignores. Investigate: does resolve_package_config or the manifest-open path already detect and special-case workspace-inheriting packages elsewhere (e.g. via CargoWorkspaceResolver at open time in a way that makes direct-path writes still work correctly), or is this a genuine correctness gap where workspace-inheriting Cargo members silently fail to get bumped? Needs real investigation (read callisto-manifests' CargoToml::write_version and WorkspaceInheritance handling) before deciding if this is a live bug needing a fix, or defensive/pre-wired-for-later infrastructure that's safe as unreachable today.

#[derive(Clone, Debug, thiserror::Error, miette::Diagnostic, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum ConfigError {
    #[error("failed to read `{path}`: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E110))]
    Read { path: PathBuf, message: String },

    #[error("`{path}` is not valid TOML: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E111), help("Verify callisto.toml TOML syntax formatting."))]
    ParseToml { path: PathBuf, message: String },

    #[error("[[package-set]] `{pattern}` matched no packages")]
    PackageSetMatchedNothing { pattern: String },

    #[error("[[package]] `{pattern}` matched no package")]
    PackageMatchedNothing { pattern: String },

    #[error("package `{package}` is claimed by more than one [[package-set]]: {}", .patterns.join(", "))]
    OverlappingPackageSets {
        package: String,
        patterns: Vec<String>,
    },

    #[error("group `{group}` and group `{other}` both list `{member}`")]
    ConflictingGroupNames {
        group: GroupName,
        other: GroupName,
        member: String,
    },

    #[error("group `{group}` has no members")]
    EmptyGroup { group: GroupName },

    #[error("duplicate group name `{group}`")]
    DuplicateGroupName { group: GroupName },

    #[error("`publish-to` names registry key `{key}`, which no [registries.*] block defines")]
    UnknownRegistry { key: String },

    #[error("`{path}` sets unknown callisto key `{key}`")]
    UnknownKey { path: PathBuf, key: String },

    #[error("`cascade.bump-severity` is `{found}`; expected `patch` or `minor`")]
    InvalidBumpSeverity { found: String },

    #[error("`pre-major-inference` is `{found}`; expected `off`, `conservative`, or `conservative-feat`")]
    InvalidPreMajorInference { found: String },

    #[error(
        "changesets.dir `{dir}` is an absolute path or contains `..` path components and would escape the workspace root"
    )]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E116),
        help("Use a forward-slash-separated path relative to the workspace root that is not absolute and does not contain '..' components.")
    )]
    InvalidChangesetsDir { dir: String },

    #[error("`changelog = \"{value}\"` on `{pattern}` is an absolute path or contains `..` path components and would escape the workspace root")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E113),
        help("Use a forward-slash-separated path relative to the package root that does not contain '..' components.")
    )]
    InvalidChangelogPath { pattern: String, value: String },

    #[error(transparent)]
    Tag(#[from] TagTemplateError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    VersionParse(#[from] VersionParseError),
}

> `--strict`/`--strict-graph` promotion (§G.11's opening paragraph); `matrix` has neither flag
> on `MatrixOptions` at all. `matrix` is a read-only discovery report consumed by CI tooling
> that expects a matrix even when some packages have manifest quirks — a workspace with one
> unrecognised triple should still emit a usable matrix for every other package, not fail the
> whole CI run on the strength of an unregistered target platform. Malformed manifest *syntax*
> (§AC-010/010b/010c) is still a hard `Err`, since there is no report to degrade to once a
> `package.json`/`pyproject.toml` doesn't parse at all — the diagnostic path exists specifically
> for the "each half parsed fine, this platform triple is merely unrecognised" case.

### G.12 Errors — `error.rs`

`LocateError` and `GraphError` are declared here, verbatim as pinned in §M.13.3. That text is
authoritative for every variant listed there; this section adds one enum and records the
`GraphError` variants that come with it.

> `[SPEC DECISION, not in 00-design.md: `GraphError` gains a `Config(#[from] ConfigError)`
> variant.]` §M.13.3 pins `GraphError`'s variants for cross-crate vocabulary agreement, and
> none of them can carry §14's config failures (a `[[package-set]]` matching nothing, an
> unknown registry key, a malformed `callisto.toml`). The enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, which is
> the mechanism for exactly this; adding a transparent wrapper rather than N variants keeps
> §M.13.3's list intact and keeps config errors namespaced. The same reasoning covers the
> `Changelog` and `Conventional` transparent wrappers §M.13.3 also lists.

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, thiserror::Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum ConfigError {
    #[error("failed to read `{path}`: {message}")]
    Read { path: PathBuf, message: String },

    #[error("`{path}` is not valid TOML: {message}")]
    ParseToml { path: PathBuf, message: String },

    /// §14. A set that matches nothing is almost always a typo'd glob, and silently ignoring
    /// it means a whole directory of packages never gets versioned.
    #[error("[[package-set]] `{pattern}` matched no packages")]
    PackageSetMatchedNothing { pattern: String },

    #[error("[[package]] `{pattern}` matched no package")]
    PackageMatchedNothing { pattern: String },

    /// §14: "two sets claiming the same package is a hard config error."
    #[error("package `{package}` is claimed by more than one [[package-set]]: {}",
            .patterns.join(", "))]
    OverlappingPackageSets { package: String, patterns: Vec<String> },

    /// §G.5.5 pass 1 — the syntactic half of §14's group validation, which runs before any
    /// discovery so a config that is wrong on its face fails on its own terms.
    #[error("group `{group}` and group `{other}` both list `{member}`")]
    ConflictingGroupNames { group: GroupName, other: GroupName, member: String },

    #[error("group `{group}` has no members")]
    EmptyGroup { group: GroupName },

    #[error("duplicate group name `{group}`")]
    DuplicateGroupName { group: GroupName },

    #[error("`publish-to` names registry key `{key}`, which no [registries.*] block defines")]
    UnknownRegistry { key: String },

    /// A typo'd override that silently does nothing is the failure P5 exists to make
    /// structural — so unknown keys under `extensions.callisto` are rejected, not ignored.
    #[error("`{path}` sets unknown callisto key `{key}`")]
    UnknownKey { path: PathBuf, key: String },

    /// §14's `[cascade].bump-severity` accepts `patch | minor` only (§G.5.4).
    #[error("`cascade.bump-severity` is `{found}`; expected `patch` or `minor`")]
    InvalidBumpSeverity { found: String },

    /// §G.5.3's three-valued key.
    #[error("`pre-major-inference` is `{found}`; expected `off`, `conservative`, or \
             `conservative-feat`")]
    InvalidPreMajorInference { found: String },

    #[error(transparent)]
    Tag(#[from] TagTemplateError),
}
```

`TagTemplateError` surfacing through `ConfigError` is deliberate: §9.1 and §M.9.1 both require
tag templates to be validated **at config-load time** (the `{version}`-exactly-once rule, the
glob-metacharacter rule, and §M.9.1's `NoLiteralAnchor` rule), because `last_tag_for` derives a
glob from the template and a template with no literal anchor would glob every tag in the
repository.

cd /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto
git status --porcelain
git add docs/01-spec.md
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
docs(spec): fix CommitInference/select_inference drift in G.6.4 and CLI sections

docs/01-spec.md's SeverityInference/CommitInference reproduction (§G.6.4)
predated commit 16eda43's GitAccess-threading fix: still showed the old
signature (no git parameter) and CommitInference as a runner/root-holding
generic struct instead of the current zero-field marker type. Fixed to
match current source exactly, and added an honest note that CommitInference
is never constructed in production -- callisto-cli hardcodes NoInference
unconditionally in both commands/version.rs and commands/compose_pr_body.rs,
with no #[cfg(feature = "inference")] branch anywhere, despite the crate
forwarding an inference Cargo feature to callisto-graph/inference.

Also fixed §CLI.6.3.1 and two adjacent pseudocode/prose spots (the
version command's main flow, and compose_pr_body's description) that
all presented a select_inference function as real callisto-cli code --
no such function, and no CommitInference::new method, exist anywhere;
grep confirms zero call sites outside infer.rs's own definition and
tests. Reworded to mark the intended design explicitly hypothetical
and describe actual current behavior (hardcoded NoInference) in the
flow-description text.

This reveals a real product gap, not just a doc bug: v0.2's milestone
commitment to wire commit-based severity inference into the CLI
(docs/01-spec.md §G.14) has never shipped, despite the workspace being
at v0.3.3. Tracked separately (task #14) as a product decision, not
resolved here.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HxMVynBHufrDkmRHgmKgcH
EOF
)"

## AC-013: WorkspaceCargoResolver source-diff unmodified

T07 commit: c736bbcfc8250c85f94c67919319c1814c5064db

Located via `git log --format=%H --grep='batch same-path Manifest-trait writes into one open/mutate/persist cycle' -1`, confirmed unique (a single matching commit; subject `fix(graph): batch same-path Manifest-trait writes into one open/mutate/persist cycle`, cross-checked with `git log --oneline | grep -i "batch same-path"`).

`git diff --name-only c736bbcfc8250c85f94c67919319c1814c5064db^ c736bbcfc8250c85f94c67919319c1814c5064db` shows T07's commit touched exactly two files: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` and `crates/callisto-graph/tests/apply_persist_open_count_test.rs`. `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` does not appear in T07's diff at all, so `WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_version` and `WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency` are unmodified by this commit.

`git diff c736bbcfc8250c85f94c67919319c1814c5064db^ c736bbcfc8250c85f94c67919319c1814c5064db -- crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs | grep -E '^-' | grep -E 'ws_res\.(write_version|write_dependency)'` produced no output -- no removed or changed line touches a `ws_res.write_version`/`ws_res.write_dependency` call site. Direct inspection of the diff hunks confirms zero lines referencing `VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage` or `DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency` appear in the diff at all (the match arms at their current locations in apply.rs, lines 204 and 232, are untouched by this commit) -- the diff's 52 added / 3 removed lines in apply.rs are confined to the new `classify_manifest_writes`-driven batching logic and the `if !classification.excluded.contains(p) { continue; }` guard around the surrounding `Manifest(p)` arms, not the CargoWorkspacePackage/CargoWorkspaceDependency arms themselves.

## AC-017: bump-before-rewrites ordering is not byte-observable, correcting T13's commit-message evidence

T13's commit (`1234bef`) recorded a blanket claim that `CargoToml::update_dependency_spec` "only touches a dependency-table entry with a plan-time-constant value, no read of `current_version()`/other state." An independent review of that commit caught that this claim is incomplete for one branch, and since commit messages cannot be corrected after the fact, the complete evidence is recorded here instead.

Read `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` directly:

- `CargoToml::write_version` (lines 200-242): touches only `[package].version` in the direct-write branch, or does an explicit pinned replacement of that same field for a workspace-inherited member. No other state is read or written. Claim holds without qualification.
- `CargoToml::update_dependency_spec` (lines 290-377): for a **non-inherited** dependency (lines 320-376, the case both of T13's AC-014/AC-016 fixtures and this file's own AC-005/AC-006 fixture exercise), the claim holds exactly as stated -- a disjoint dependency-table entry is mutated with a plan-time-constant `DepSpec`, no read of `current_version()`. For an **inherited** dependency (lines 305-318), the method instead delegates to `WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_cargo)` followed by `ws_res.write_dependency(name, new, permit)` -- an immediate, synchronous read-and-persist against a **different physical file** (the workspace root `Cargo.toml`), not the manifest whose handle `update_dependency_spec` was called on. `WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency` calls `self.persist(permit)` internally (cargo.rs:709), and `WorkspaceCargoResolver::persist` (cargo.rs:715-723) does not call `crate::record_persist_call()`, so this delegated write is invisible to `persist_call_count()`.

This does not weaken AC-017's actual claim: the delegated write lands on a file distinct from the one being batched in the group under discussion, so it has no bearing on whether bump-before-rewrites ordering is byte-observable *within that group's own manifest*. It also does not contradict this spec's own scope: `non_goals` already states that `WorkspaceCargoResolver`-routed writes remain immediate, per-entry, and outside `persist_call_count`'s instrumentation (which is scoped exclusively to the `Manifest` trait's three implementors). The correction here is one of completeness in T13's evidence write-up, not a functional defect in the shipped code -- verified via `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib apply::tests` (22 passed) and `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean) after this note was added, confirming no code change was needed or made.

input.description: docs/01-spec.md's §CM section (crates/callisto-manifests spec, around line 3908-3936, search "Writes are refused and redirected") claims CargoToml::write_version refuses with ManifestError::WorkspaceInherited on a workspace-inheriting member, requiring the caller to redirect to WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_version instead ("The correct target for *any* member whose write_version refused with WorkspaceInherited { key: "version", .. }"). This contradicts real source: crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs's write_version (lines 210-228) does NOT refuse for a workspace-inheriting member -- it explicitly pins an explicit version string directly into the member's own [package] section, replacing the inherited declaration, without touching the workspace root at all. This is deliberate and tested (write_version_pins_explicitly_on_workspace_inheriting_member, cargo.rs:1567). Only current_version() refuses with WorkspaceInherited, and only when no resolved inheritance context was supplied at open() time (a different, narrower condition than what write_version's own paragraph claims). Investigate the full scope of this section's drift (does update_dependency_spec's own described "refused and redirected" claim hold, per crates/callisto-graph/tests/apply_batch_002_verification_notes.md's AC-017 finding that update_dependency_spec DOES delegate to WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency for an inherited dependency -- unlike write_version, which does not delegate at all) before rewriting the section, since the two methods may have genuinely different real behavior that the doc currently conflates.

   predecessor (determinism, §G.7.5); a graph engineered to require exactly `3n` raises,
   asserting `iterations ≤ convergence_bound(n)`.
3. **Peer escalation into a fixed group.** The §G.7.5 case: two fixed members, one
   peer-escalated to `Major`, asserting both end at `Major` and that no `FixedGroupDivergent` is
   raised. This is the fixture that would fail if `raise` were not group-aware.
4. **Linked-group joint vs. cascade.** Two linked members at different base versions: (a) both
   named → shared max version (§G.6.7); (b) one named, the other reached only by cascade →
   independent version lines, no union; (c) one named `none`, one named `minor` → joint, both
   `minor` (§G.6.6).

   `workspace:*`, `catalog:default`, `^1 || ^2`, against a bump — asserting precision
   preservation, `LeftAlone` for the last, and that every `Rewritten` output re-parses and
   re-covers (§G.7.7's verification).

Also run `cargo test -p callisto-cli --lib` (default, no inference feature) yourself and confirm 48 tests pass with the new test correctly absent (not run, not failing) from that build.
5. Run `cargo clippy -p callisto-cli --all-targets --features inference -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p callisto-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` yourself (both feature configurations) and confirm both clean.
6. Sibling-gap check: grep the whole `callisto-cli` crate for any OTHER hardcoded `NoInference` construction that this fix might have missed (besides the two already-fixed call sites in version.rs and compose_pr_body.rs) -- e.g. other commands, other binaries, or a `main.rs` entry point that might also need this wiring.
7. Check whether removing the now-unused `use callisto_graph::infer::NoInference;` top-level imports from `version.rs` and `compose_pr_body.rs` was done cleanly (no leftover unused-import warnings, and confirm the test module's own separate/local `NoInference` import for its two pre-existing tests, `version_text_output_includes_package_name_and_versions` and `version_json_output_is_valid_json_with_expected_structure`, is unaffected and those tests still pass).

**CLI.6.3.1 — `SeverityInference` selection, *intended* to be milestone-gated by Cargo feature:**

This was the plan; it has not shipped. `callisto-cli` does forward an `inference` Cargo
feature to `callisto-graph/inference` (`Cargo.toml`), but no command handler consults it —
`commands/version.rs` and `commands/compose_pr_body.rs` both hardcode `let inference =
NoInference;` unconditionally, with no `#[cfg(feature = "inference")]` branch anywhere in
either file. Enabling `--features inference` on `callisto-cli` today compiles
`callisto_graph::infer::CommitInference` into the dependency tree but nothing ever selects it,
so it has no effect on the binary's behavior. The `select_inference` function below never
existed in real code; it describes the intended shape, not a call site that was removed:

```rust
// INTENDED (§17, §G.14) -- not implemented in callisto-cli as of this writing.
#[cfg(not(feature = "inference"))]
fn select_inference(_: &Workspace<'_, …>) -> impl SeverityInference {
    callisto_graph::infer::NoInference
}

#[cfg(feature = "inference")]
fn select_inference<'a>(ws: &'a Workspace<'a, …>) -> impl SeverityInference + 'a {
    callisto_graph::infer::CommitInference
}
```

> `[SPEC DECISION, not in 00-design.md: the concrete `SeverityInference` impl is selected
> behind a Cargo feature (`inference`) rather than a runtime branch.]` §17 v0.1 ships
> `callisto-graph` with `infer::NoInference` and defers "`infer` wired to
> `callisto-conventional`" to v0.2 explicitly — a v0.1 binary that unconditionally linked the
> inference path would ship dead code for a milestone. The feature flag is the smallest
> mechanism consistent with P4's bounded-work promise: v0.2's binary flips the default-features
> list, no handler code changes. The impl itself is `callisto-graph`'s, not this crate's
> (§G.6.4) — an earlier draft placed it in `callisto-conventional`, which cannot see the trait;
> §11 records the reconciliation. As the paragraph above notes, this decision was made but the
> handler-side wiring it describes was never actually implemented.

3911	    /// call here typically satisfies every such member for the run, which is the entire point
3912	    /// of the Cargo feature this resolves (§18 Q2).
3913	    pub fn write_version(&mut self, v: &Version) -> Result<(), ManifestError>;

input.old_string:
**Reads are transparent; writes are refused and redirected.** A member `CargoToml` opened
with `ctx.cargo_workspace = Some(inheritance)` answers `current_version()` and
`iter_dependencies()` with the *real, resolved* values — a caller reading a member's version
or dependency list never needs to know inheritance was involved. Only a *write* attempt
directly on the member surfaces `WorkspaceInherited`, because that is the one operation where
"which file actually gets edited" matters and getting it wrong (writing a local override) is a
silent correctness bug, not merely redundant work.

**Reads are transparent; the two write methods handle inheritance differently, and neither
surfaces `WorkspaceInherited`.** A member `CargoToml` opened with `ctx.cargo_workspace =
Some(inheritance)` answers `current_version()` and `iter_dependencies()` with the *real,
resolved* values — a caller reading a member's version or dependency list never needs to know
inheritance was involved. Grep of `callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` confirms
`ManifestError::WorkspaceInherited` is constructed in exactly one place, and it's not a write
path at all: `current_version()`, when `self.inherited_version` is set but no
`WorkspaceCargoResolver` context was ever supplied to `open()` — a caller-contract violation
caught the first time anyone tries to read the version, not a "which file gets edited" signal.

`write_version` on an inherited member never touches the root and never errors: it writes an
explicit pinned version string directly into the member's own `[package]` section, replacing
the inheritance declaration (tested by

an inherited dependency instead delegates transparently — it loads a
`WorkspaceCargoResolver` for the root and calls `write_dependency` itself, with no error
surfaced to its own caller — *unless* the manifest being edited **is** the workspace root
itself, in which case it refuses with `ManifestError::InvariantViolation` (not
`WorkspaceInherited`) to avoid overwriting the just-written root with a stale in-memory
document.

message.content: Should we have used opus for anything though? Why didn't you think through quality with a mind on cost too?

content.text:
Fair critique — I didn't actually reason through it, I just defaulted to "omit `model`, inherit session" without asking whether this specific task warranted an upgrade. That's not the same as deciding Sonnet was right.

Here's the tradeoff I should have made explicit:

- **Survey stage** (find candidate gaps): Sonnet is probably fine here — it's read-heavy, pattern-matching work (does this function exist, does this signature match), not deep judgment.
- **Verify stage** (adversarially refute each claimed gap): this is the one place a same-tier verifier checking a same-tier surveyor's work has a real weakness — correlated blind spots. If Sonnet's survey pass missed a subtlety or misread a code path, a Sonnet verify pass is more likely to share that same gap in reasoning than an independent, stronger model would be. This is exactly the kind of "second opinion" role where bumping to Opus is a well-motivated call, not just a quality flex — it's specifically about decorrelating the error.
- **Synthesis** (write the final report): lower stakes — it's organizing already-verified findings, not generating new judgment. Sonnet is fine here.

Cost-wise: survey is a fixed 12 calls regardless of model. Verify calls scale with however many gaps get found (unknown count until survey finishes), so that's where an Opus upgrade would actually move the cost needle — but it's also the stage where it matters most for catching real bugs vs. false-clears.

Let me check where the workflow actually is before deciding whether to change anything.

lastPrompt: If you switch thw workflow to opus do we eat the cost of all of the context from all 123 agents being laoded into opus though?? That is expensive

content.text:
Good instinct to check, but no — that's not how it works. Two things are true here that avoid the blowup you're worried about:

**1. Agents don't inherit each other's context.** Every `agent()` call in the workflow — survey or verify — spawns a fresh, independent subagent with its own small context window: just the prompt string I wrote for that one call, plus whatever it reads itself via its own Read/Grep calls. A verify agent's prompt is maybe a few hundred words (the specific gap description, citation, expected/actual, evidence) — it never sees the other ~120 agents' transcripts, outputs, or reasoning. There's no accumulation happening across agents; that's the entire design point of fan-out — it keeps each agent's context small on purpose, not shared.

**2. Resuming with an edited script doesn't replay finished work.** Right now the run is at 65 started / 55 completed (survey is done, verify is well underway). If I resume with `model: 'opus'` added only to the verify stage, the cache matches on `(prompt, opts)` — survey calls are unchanged, so they hit cache and cost nothing to re-fetch. Only the verify calls (whose opts now differ) actually re-run. So the real cost delta is:

**(number of verify calls, not 123) × (that one small independent prompt's tokens, at Opus rate instead of Sonnet rate)**

Not "123 agents' worth of context, now billed at Opus rates." The only place anything gets concatenated across agents at all is the final synthesis step, where I pass the *already-distilled* findings list (short JSON, not raw transcripts) into one single Sonnet call — and that stays on Sonnet regardless.

So the actual cost question is just: is (~50-70ish verify calls) × (Opus rate vs Sonnet rate) worth it for the decorrelation benefit? That's a real number, just a much smaller and more bounded one than what you were picturing.

pub struct StatusReport {
    pub schema_version: u32,
    /// Mandatory (§12.5) — the field the Action's mode dispatch reads.
    pub has_changesets: bool,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub packages: Vec<StatusEntry>,
    ...
}
```
i.e. non-optional, always-serialized (no `skip_serializing_if`), exactly as claimed. §12.5 (docs/00-design.md:1161) independently corroborates: `status` → `.hasChangesets` (mandatory)`, and §12.2 branch 3 (docs/00-design.md:1100) says the Action dispatches on `callisto status --format json` → `.hasChangesets`.

**Code side** (`crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:298-306`, exact cited range): the real struct is
```rust
pub struct StatusReport {
    pub schema_version: u32,
    pub packages: Vec<StatusPackageRecord>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>,
}
```
No `has_changesets` field. Workspace-wide grep for `has_changesets`/`hasChangesets` across `crates/` returns zero matches (confirmed independently) — only appears in `docs/00-design.md`, `docs/01-spec.md`, and `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`. There is no alternate code path, wrapper `Serialize` impl, or `cfg`-gated field that supplies it: `output.rs::write_json`/`write_report_json` serialize the struct as-is with no field injection, and both constructors of `StatusReport` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/status.rs:105`, and the CLI's own test helper) only ever populate `schema_version`/`packages`/`diagnostics`.

The closest related code is `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/status.rs`'s private `check_exit_code_raw(&StatusReport) -> u8`, which computes an equivalent boolean internally (`packages.iter().any(|p| !p.pending_changesets.is_empty())`) — but this is never serialized into the JSON output; it's used only to pick an exit code for the `--check` flag. I also traced the actual GitHub composite action (`.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml:88-99`) and found it does NOT read `.hasChangesets` from the JSON at all — it shells out to `callisto status --check` and branches on the raw process exit code instead (and even that exit-code convention appears mismatched: the Rust code's exit-code comment says 1=pending/2=not-pending, while the action script checks for 0=pending/2=not-pending — a separate, unrelated inconsistency I'm flagging only as context, not as part of this claim). This confirms the JSON contract described in the spec was never implemented in code, in any form.

1	# Callisto Workspace Spec-Conformance Audit — Final Report
2	
3	## Executive Summary
4	
5	A full adversarial audit checked **870 claims** across the entire Callisto Rust workspace against `docs/00-design.md` and `docs/01-spec.md`. **684 claims (78.6%) confirmed correct**; **115 claims (13.2%) confirmed as genuine spec-vs-code gaps**, each independently re-verified against real code and spec text before being logged here. Every finding below is a **CONFIRMED** gap, not a suspicion.
6	
7	The most consequential findings cluster around **`callisto-graph`'s version-orchestration core**: a real (non-dry-run) `callisto snapshot` currently stages a transient fake version into the git index (data-loss risk), fixed-group version alignment and platform-manifest/optionalDependencies writes are entirely unimplemented, dependency resolution can silently fabricate cross-ecosystem edges, and peer-dependency escalation ignores the true cascade source severity — several of these are **critical, reachable-today correctness bugs**, not just documentation drift. A second major theme is **structural/architectural non-conformance**: `callisto-cli` depends on the manifest-writing crate it's explicitly forbidden to depend on, the `callisto-moon` WASM extension implements only 2 of ~10 documented subcommands (silently falling back to `status` for everything else, contradicting its own "fails loudly" guarantee), and large swaths of the `callisto-fixtures` shared-test-infrastructure crate (GraphBuilder, ScenarioBuilder, ReplayCommandRunner, the entire `data/` corpus) simply do not exist. A third theme is pervasive **JSON output-contract drift** in `callisto-model`'s report types (missing/renamed fields across `StatusReport`, `SnapshotReport`, `ComposePrBodyReport`, `ValidateReport`, `CreatedTag`, `InitReport`).
8	
9	**Severity breakdown:** 15 Critical · 44 High · 38 Medium · 18 Low (115 total).
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Critical Severity (15)
14	
15	### callisto-model
16	
17	**1. `callisto-model` performs real filesystem I/O, contradicting the crate's explicit "no I/O" invariant.**
18	- Spec: §M.1.2 (line 192) — "This crate performs no filesystem, process, or network I/O... it implements neither."
19	- Expected: Zero `std::fs`/`std::process`/network calls; only trait declarations and value types.
20	- Actual: `atomic_write` performs unconditional real I/O (create_dir_all, tempfile write/flush/sync_all, parent/grandparent dir fsync); the whole `atomic`/`permit`/`registry`/`commit`/`matrix` module set is absent from the spec's module layout.
21	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-model/src/atomic.rs:42-69`; module layout at `docs/01-spec.md:228-253`.
22	
23	**2. `StatusReport` is missing the spec-mandated `hasChangesets` field entirely.**
24	- Spec: §M.12.4 (lines 1867-1879) — `has_changesets: bool` is mandatory, "the field the Action's mode dispatch reads."
25	- Expected: A mandatory (non-optional, always-serialized) `has_changesets: bool` field.
26	- Actual: `StatusReport` has only `schema_version`, `packages`, `diagnostics`. Zero workspace matches for `has_changesets`/`hasChangesets`.
27	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:298-306`.
28	
29	### callisto-changelog
30	
31	**3. `compose-pr-body` never calls `callisto-changelog`'s `render_section` at all**, building an entirely independent, hand-rolled Markdown report instead — contradicting the spec's central "one render function, three consumers" decision.
32	- Spec: §CL.2 (~L4898-4910) SPEC DECISION: one render function, three consumers, never three independent renderings; §CL.7.2 (~L5189-5200).
33	- Expected: `render_pr_body_from_plan` calls `callisto_changelog::render_section(&ChangelogInput)` and wraps output in `<details><summary>package@version</summary>`.
34	- Actual: `pr_body.rs` never imports `callisto_changelog`; builds its own table/bullets from `BumpReason`. `render_section` has exactly one production caller in the whole workspace (`apply.rs:241`).
35	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/pr_body.rs:1-242`.
36	
37	**4. `plan_publish` never reads the CHANGELOG.md section back**; `ReleaseEntry.changelog_section` is unconditionally hardcoded to `None`.
38	- Spec: §CL.7.1 (~L5149-5188) three-case table incl. `DiagnosticCode::ChangelogSectionNotFound`; §M.16 decision 23.
39	- Expected: `plan_publish` calls `extract_section(&contents, &released_version)` to populate `changelog_section`, emitting a Warning diagnostic when missing.
40	- Actual: `changelog_section: None` hardcoded; `extract_section`/`ChangelogSectionNotFound` never called/constructed anywhere in `callisto-graph`/`callisto-cli`.
41	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs:427`.
42	
43	### callisto-graph (discovery/config)
44	
45	**5. `[[package]]`/`[[package-set]] match` is matched against the package's NAME, not its workspace-relative directory path** — every path-glob example in the design doc's own `callisto.toml` sample would match zero packages.
46	- Spec: `docs/00-design.md:1354-1374`; `docs/01-spec.md:6302-6322` (§G.5.1 defines `match` against `P`, the package's root path).
47	- Expected: `match` compared against a package's workspace-relative root path.
48	- Actual: `PackageId::parse`/`PackagePattern::matches` glob-match against `id.name()`, never `rel_path`. Following the docs' own `match = "crates/*"` example matches zero real packages.
49	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:349`; `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/pattern.rs:53-71`; `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:175,182,194`.
50	
51	**6. Dependency-edge resolution silently falls back to a cross-ecosystem name match**, directly contradicting the spec's own worked example ("a Cargo `serde` dependency must not resolve to an npm workspace member called `serde`").
52	- Spec: §G.4.2 (~L6049-6068); §G.4.4 step (b) (~L6168-6169).
53	- Expected: A same-ecosystem-only lookup miss must be dropped as external, never wired to a same-named package in a different ecosystem.
54	- Actual: `resolve_native_with_fallback` scans all other ecosystems and silently returns a single cross-ecosystem candidate with no diagnostic; wired into real edge extraction and locked in by a passing test.
55	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/identity.rs:314-338,343-392`; `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:360-364`.
56	
57	**7. `IgnoreWalkLocator::projects()` never implements Cargo `[workspace]` members/exclude or npm `"workspaces"`/`pnpm-workspace.yaml` filtering**, so intentionally-excluded crates (fuzz targets, scratch examples) are discovered and treated as real release-managed packages.
58	- Spec: §G.2.2 steps 1 and 4 (~L5740-5761).
59	- Expected: Discovery reads workspace membership globs and drops non-surviving candidates.
60	- Actual: No membership-filter step exists anywhere in `projects()`.
61	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs:38-142`.
62	
63	**8. `moon.yml`'s `extensions.callisto` block — documented as the highest-precedence config layer — is never actually deserialized from any file anywhere in the workspace.**
64	- Spec: §G.5.1 (~L6284-6285); §G.5.2 SPEC DECISION (~L6366-6376).
65	- Expected: `callisto-graph` reads each project's `moon.yml` `extensions.callisto` YAML directly as the highest-precedence config layer.
66	- Actual: `RawMoonYml`/`RawMoonExtensions`/`RawMoonCallistoConfig` are declared but never constructed; `callisto-graph` has no YAML dependency at all; `walk.rs`'s config-application logic only consults `[[package]]`/`[[package-set]]`.
67	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/raw.rs:116-145`; no `serde_yaml` dependency in `Cargo.toml`.
68	
69	### callisto-graph (aggregation/cascade/groups)
70	
71	**9. A real `callisto snapshot` run unconditionally `git add`s the transient snapshot-versioned manifests**, because `ApplyOptions::transient` (and all suppression logic built around it) has been removed from the codebase entirely — a data-loss regression the spec explicitly designed this flag to prevent.
72	- Spec: §G.10.2 ApplyOptions.transient doc (~L8110-8115) + dedicated SPEC DECISION (~L8188-8206): "staging them would put a transient version into the next `git commit -a` a human runs. That is data loss, not a policy difference."
73	- Expected: Step 11 (`git add`) — along with steps 7/8 — must be skipped in snapshot mode.
74	- Actual: `ApplyOptions` now only has `refresh_lockfiles`; the final staging block in `apply.rs` is fully unconditional. Empirically reproduced: a real `callisto snapshot` run leaves the transient `0.0.0-<tag>-<sha>` version staged in the git index.
75	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:16-20,407-443`; `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/snapshot.rs:38-46`.
76	
77	**10. Fixed-group members never delegate to `fixed_group_target`** — the function exists and is exported but has zero call sites; a new fixed-group member bumps from its own on-disk base (e.g. `0.0.1`) instead of the group's aligned target.
78	- Spec: §G.7.4 `bump_target` doc (~L7457-7466).
79	- Expected: `bump_target` checks fixed-group membership and delegates to `fixed_group_target` for aligned versioning.
80	- Actual: No group-membership check exists in `bump_target` at all; `fixed_group_target` is dead code.
81	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:387-419`; `crates/callisto-graph/src/groups.rs:97`.
82	
83	**11. §7.6 steps 4-5 (platform-manifest writes with parent's version, and updating napi main packages' `optionalDependencies` to exact platform versions) are entirely unimplemented.**
84	- Spec: §G.10.1 (~L8020-8024); §G.10.2 steps 4-5 (~L8162-8163).
85	- Expected: `apply_version_plan` dispatches `plan.platform_writes`/`plan.optional_dep_updates` to real writes; `update_optional_dependencies` (already implemented in `callisto-manifests`) gets called.
86	- Actual: `apply.rs` has zero references to either field/type; every planner hardcodes `platform_writes: Vec::new()` / `optional_dep_updates: Vec::new()`.
87	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`; `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:249-250`, `snapshot.rs:132-133`, `pr_body.rs:282-283,303-304`.
88	
89	**12. Peer-dependency escalation to Major ignores the cascading dependency's own source severity**, so an out-of-range peer spec is escalated to Major even when the upstream change was only a Patch, with `peer_escalation = true` the documented default.
90	- Spec: §G.7.1 rows 4/5 (~L7160-7168, ~L7213-7215); `docs/00-design.md` L1265 (invariant 9: "non-patch escalates to major").
91	- Expected: Escalation only when `cfg.peer_escalation && source is Minor|Major`; a Patch-source out-of-range peer edge falls through to the ordinary bump-severity row.
92	- Actual: `cascade_action`'s parameter is `_source: Severity` (unused); the Peer/DoesNotCover arm never inspects it — every out-of-range Peer edge escalates to Major regardless of true source severity.
93	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:26,49-53`.
94	
95	**13. Dependency-spec rewrite keys are built from `PackageId::name()` instead of `IdentityIndex::native_name`**, so cascade-driven rewrites target the wrong manifest key for any cross-ecosystem edge onto a dual-identity (napi) package — exactly the failure mode `RewriteKey::of` was spec'd to prevent.
96	- Spec: §G.7.3, `RewriteKey::of` (~L7289-7317).
97	- Expected: The dependency-table key is obtained via `IdentityIndex::native_name(&edge.to, eco)`.
98	- Actual: No `RewriteKey::of` exists; `solve_cascade` builds the key inline via `edge.to.name().to_string()`, which returns the wrong ecosystem's native name for Case-D packages.
99	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:251-275`.
100	
101	### callisto-moon
102	
103	**14. `execute_extension` implements only 2 of ~10 documented commands (`plan-publish`, `validate`)** — every other subcommand (add, version, pre enter/exit, snapshot, init, tag, compose-pr-body) and any typo silently falls back to running `status` with `exit_code: 0`.
104	- Spec: MO.2.3 ("Every non-completions subcommand... dispatched to the identical `commands::` function"); MO.8's command-surface table.
105	- Expected: Each documented subcommand dispatches to its own `callisto_graph::commands::` function.
106	- Actual: The `_` fallback arm runs `commands::status` and returns success for everything unrecognized. Confirmed as intended behavior by the crate's own test, whose doc comment admits "no distinct unrecognized-subcommand error path exists today."
107	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-moon/src/extension.rs:182-241`; `crates/callisto-moon/tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs:665-739`.
108	
109	**15. The spec's own stated safety guarantee — that an unrecognized/out-of-sync subcommand "fails loudly and structurally" — is directly contradicted; it silently succeeds as `status`.**
110	- Spec: MO.2.3 — "An unrecognized subcommand name produces a report-shaped error object rather than a panic... fails loudly and structurally."
111	- Expected: A report-shaped error object with non-zero exit code.
112	- Actual: `resolve_subcommand`'s own doc comment says it "does not validate" the name; the fallback runs `status` with `exit_code: 0` and no `error` field. Reconfirmed end-to-end by a test asserting exactly this for `["totally-bogus-subcommand"]`.
113	- Evidence: `crates/callisto-moon/src/extension.rs:140-142,216-240`.
114	
115	---
116	
117	## High Severity (44)
118	
119	### callisto-model (4)
120	
121	**16.** `StatusReport.packages[]` is missing 2 of 7 documented fields (`last_released_version`, `release_trigger`), and the one field spec calls specifically mandatory (`changed_since_last_tag`) is conditionally omitted via `skip_serializing_if`. Spec: §M.12.4 (L1886-1910). Evidence: `crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:320-336`.
122	
123	**17.** `SnapshotReport`'s shape bears no resemblance to spec: no `version: Version` field, no `packages: Vec<SnapshotPackage>` — instead has `snapshot_tag: String`/`bumps: Vec<BumpRecord>`; `SnapshotPackage` doesn't exist anywhere. Spec: §M.12.5 (L1926-1949). Evidence: `crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:339-348`.
124	
125	**18.** `ComposePrBodyReport` is missing the entire spec-mandated `PrBodyMetadata`/`PrBodyOverflow` label-reconciliation contract, and `body` was renamed to `pr_body` (wire key `prBody`). Spec: §M.12.5 (L1953-2003). Evidence: `crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:363-371`.
126	
127	**19.** `CreatedTag` lacks the spec-mandated `already_existed: bool` field; the real call site that computes exactly this fact discards it, and no comparison of an existing tag's sha vs. the release sha exists anywhere — the idempotence-observability guarantee is unreachable end-to-end. Spec: §M.12.6 (L2045-2054). Evidence: `crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:431-437`; `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs:82-124`.
128	
129	### callisto-format (3)
130	
131	**20.** `versioning_for` — spec calls it "load-bearing" and required for every caller — is never called anywhere in the workspace; `callisto-graph` reimplements grammar dispatch ad hoc in two places, both losing the `None → BumpError::UnsupportedGrammar` safety path. Reachable impact: a fixed group of Pep440-grammar packages silently fails to bump instead of using the correct versioning impl. Spec: §F.6.1 (~L3138-3144). Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:398-401`; `crates/callisto-graph/src/groups.rs:137`.
132	
133	**21.** `parse_changeset`/`write_changeset` enforce an undocumented `EmptySummary` hard error (absent from the spec's claimed-exhaustive error enums), which pre-empts `callisto-graph`'s own independently-implemented, more graceful `EmptySummary` diagnostic — making that diagnostic path permanently unreachable. Spec: §F.5.5/§F.5.6 (L2994-3103). Evidence: `crates/callisto-format/src/changeset/mod.rs:107-113,124-127,191-196,218-223`.
134	
135	**22.** The entire fixture-corpus test strategy §F.9 describes (vendored `@changesets/cli` fixtures, `cases.toml`, golden tables, provenance headers) does not exist; `callisto-format` doesn't even depend on `callisto-fixtures` as its spec-declared dev-dependency. Spec: §F.9 (L3418-3477). Evidence: `crates/callisto-format/Cargo.toml:25-27`; no `data/` directory anywhere.
136	
137	### callisto-manifests (3)
138	
139	**23.** The `Manifest` trait's real signature and persistence model diverge completely from spec, which claims it's "reproduced exactly" with auto-persisting mutating methods. Real trait adds an `ApplyPermit` parameter, a required separate `persist()` method, and two undocumented methods (`is_publishable`, `publish_targets`) — writes do NOT auto-persist, confirmed by dedicated tests. Spec: `docs/01-spec.md:3543-3586`. Evidence: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs:26-63`.
140	
141	**24.** Python/`pyproject.toml` is claimed "demand-gated, not implemented" but is a complete, tested, **default-on**, end-to-end-wired ecosystem (1680-line implementation, 42+ tests, live in identity resolution/discovery/matrix generation). Spec: CM.7/CM.8 (L4172-4222). Evidence: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs`; `crates/callisto-manifests/Cargo.toml:14` (`default = ["cargo", "npm", "pypi"]`).
142	
143	**25.** Building with only the `npm` feature fails to compile with 39 E0433 errors, contradicting the spec's claim that a disabled format is a "compile-time impossibility" handled cleanly — `pub mod cargo;`/`pub mod python;` are not feature-gated despite referencing `toml_edit`, which is only pulled in by other features. Spec: CM.2 (L3641-3645). Evidence: `cargo check -p callisto-manifests --no-default-features --features npm` (39 errors); `crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs:14,17`.
144

Spec: §13.1.1. Evidence: `crates/callisto-graph/src/resolver.rs:27-34`; `crates/callisto-graph/src/toposort.rs:78-95`.
