# Callisto Runtime & Performance Audit

*Follow-up to the static spec-vs-code audit (115 confirmed gaps: 15 critical, 44 high, 38 medium, 18 low). This pass ran the compiled `callisto` binary against constructed scenarios to validate the critical/high static findings live, swept for runtime-only defects the static read couldn't see, and measured performance at scale.*

## 1. Executive Summary

Of the 59 critical/high static findings assigned for runtime validation, 56 were reproduced with a real command against a real workspace and real output, 2 were pure code/config facts with no meaningful separate runtime repro (confirmed via `cargo tree`, `find`, and compiler errors instead), and 1 produced a genuine discrepancy between the static finding and the initial runtime attempt — resolved, after independent re-verification, in favor of the **original static finding**: the runtime attempt's "unreachable in practice" conclusion was itself wrong, and a live end-to-end repro of the original bug was produced. Beyond validation, this pass confirmed 21 new runtime-only issues never caught by the static read, three of them critical, including a broken release-automation contract that makes the shipped GitHub Action's primary release-PR path unreachable in production, and a version-engine bug that lets "fixed" package groups silently and permanently drift apart in version number. A performance sweep confirmed 8 real findings, mostly in the O(N_packages × repo-history) shape, with real timings measured on synthetic repos; several severities were recalibrated up or down from the initial claims once actual numbers were in hand.

The single most load-bearing result for trusting this audit going forward: adversarial re-verification caught and reversed a false negative from a *first-pass* runtime attempt. That attempt tested one scenario, got a clean result, and over-generalized it into "this bug is structurally unreachable." A second, more careful pass found the real reachable path within minutes. Treat any single negative runtime result in isolation with caution; the confirmed positives below were each independently reproduced from scratch, not merely accepted from source text.

## 2. Runtime Validation of Static Findings

### 2.1 Coverage by crate

| Crate / lane | Findings validated | Live-reproduced | Code-fact (no repro needed) | Discrepancy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| callisto-model | 6 | 6 | – | – |
| callisto-format | 3 | 2 | 1 | – |
| callisto-manifests | 3 | 3 | – | – |
| callisto-conventional | 2 | 2 | – | – |
| callisto-changelog | 7 | 6 | 1 | – |
| callisto-graph (discovery/config) | 7 | 6 | – | 1 |
| callisto-graph (aggregation/cascade/groups) | 7 | 7 | – | – |
| callisto-graph (commands/errors/fixtures) | 4 | 4 | – | – |
| callisto-cli | 3 | 3 | – | – |
| callisto-moon | 4 | 4 | – | – |
| callisto-fixtures | 7 | 7 | – | – |
| callisto-vcs | 1 | 1 | – | – |
| cross-cutting | 5 | 5 | – | – |
| **Total** | **59** | **56** | **2** | **1** |

The 2 code-facts (a nonexistent fixture-corpus test architecture in `callisto-format`, and a nonexistent wasm CI job for `callisto-changelog`) are structural absences — nothing to execute differently at runtime — and were still cross-checked with `cargo tree`/`find`/real test-suite runs rather than accepted from a source read alone.

### 2.2 Notable live confirmations

A representative sample of what "reproduced" means in this pass — these are all real command + real output, not inference from source:

- **Snapshot staging is a real data-loss vector.** A non-dry-run `callisto snapshot --tag canary` staged fabricated `0.0.0-canary-<sha>` versions directly into the git index (`git diff --cached` showed the change staged); a routine `git commit -a` afterward would commit the fake version into real history.
- **A new fixed-group member bumps from its own base, not the group's target.** A released member at `1.5.0` and a brand-new member at `0.0.0`, both in the same fixed group, ended up on disk at `1.6.0` and `0.1.0` respectively after one `callisto version` run — no error, no diagnostic.
- **Cross-ecosystem dependency rewrites can hard-crash `version`.** A Cargo/npm co-located package (Cargo name `native-core`, npm name `@myorg/native-core`) caused `callisto version` to exit 1 with `E017: has no Runtime dependency named 'native-core'` against a completely ordinary napi-style monorepo layout.
- **`callisto tag` can silently no-op while claiming success.** Re-running `tag --plan` against an already-existing tag at a different sha produced identical JSON output to the successful creation run, with the real git ref left untouched — no diagnostic, exit 0.
- **A pure-Python workspace is invisible without an unrelated moon marker.** `callisto status` on a pyproject.toml-only repo failed with `E030: workspace root not found`; creating an empty `.moon/` directory (no other change) made it work.
- **No git-version preflight exists.** A shimmed `git` reporting version `1.8.5` (below the documented `>=2.20` floor) produced normal, successful output from `status`/`version` — no capability check runs anywhere in the dispatch path.

### 2.3 Confirmed discrepancy: `ConflictingGroupMembership` is reachable after all

**Finding under test:** the static audit flagged `GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership` as declared but never constructed — the spec-mandated check for two group-member spellings colliding on the same package (`foo` vs `cargo/foo`) that should hard-error instead of silently letting one group overwrite the other's membership.

**What the first runtime attempt found:** testing the finding's literal example (`foo` vs `cargo:foo` against an ordinary Cargo package) produced a hard `E108: not found in the workspace` error, not a silent overwrite. The attempt traced this to `IdentityIndex.prefixed` never being populated in production — every real package ID is constructed as `PackageId::Bare`, so any ecosystem-prefixed spelling in a group member list fails to resolve at all. It concluded the original bug was "currently unreachable in practice."

**Why that conclusion was wrong, and how it was caught:** independent re-verification traced `resolve_human` more carefully (`identity.rs:257-261`) and found it checks bare-name *values*, not just the dead `prefixed` map. Because callisto performs zero validation on manifest name fields, a package whose declared name is itself prefix-parseable — e.g. an npm `package.json` literally named `"cargo/foo"` — enters the `bare` map as `PackageId::Prefixed`, at which point the plain string `"foo"` and the prefixed string `"cargo/foo"` resolve to the same `PackageId`. Building that exact scenario (an npm package named `cargo/foo`, two fixed groups, one referencing `foo` and the other `cargo/foo`) reproduced the original bug live: `callisto status` exits 0 with **no error**, and `GroupTable::resolve` does a bare `insert` with no conflict check — last-write-wins, one group's membership silently overwrites the other's. Escalating further, a changeset-driven `callisto version --dry-run` on that fixture produced a real invariant violation on disk: one group member left unbumped while its sibling bumped, with exit 0 throughout.

**Verdict:** the original static finding is **CONFIRMED** — `ConflictingGroupMembership` is genuinely dead code and the check is genuinely reachable and missing, with real downstream harm. The first runtime attempt's narrow negative result (on the specific example scenario it tried) was accurate on its own terms but got generalized into a false "structurally unreachable" claim. Its incidental discovery — that `IdentityIndex.prefixed` is separately dead code, making the *documented* `cargo:foo` spelling always a hard error — is real and is logged separately below as its own issue, but is a sibling bug, not a mitigation of the original one.

**Takeaway for trusting this report:** every other "not applicable" / negative result in this pass was independently re-derived, not accepted from a single attempt — this is the one case where that discipline visibly mattered.

## 3. New Runtime-Only Issues

21 issues were found during this pass that were not present in the static audit — surfaced by actually running scenarios, not by reading source. Severities below reflect the calibrated conclusion after adversarial verification, noted where it moved from the original claim.

### Critical (3)

**`callisto status --check`'s exit-code contract is inverted in the shipped release pipeline.** The compiled CLI's real `--check` contract (confirmed by both the binary's own behavior and its unit tests) is: exit 1 when changesets are pending, exit 2 when none are pending — it never returns 0. The shipped `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml` branches on `-eq 0` for "has pending changesets" and treats anything else but `2` as a hard failure. Live repro: with a real pending changeset, running the action's verbatim bash block against the real binary printed `::error::callisto status --check failed with exit code 1` and hard-exited the step — the "create/update the release PR" path is unreachable in every real run where it should fire. A second, independently-discovered defect compounds this: clap's own usage-error exit code (`2`) collides with the "no changesets pending" branch, so a CLI argument typo is silently reinterpreted as "workspace clean" and falls into the publish path — fail-open on an irreversible operation. *Category: correctness / output-contract.*

**Fixed-group safety checks are fully built, unit-tested, and never called from any real command.** `pre_mutation_checks`, `fixed_group_target`, and `napi_drift` — the functions that force-align a fixed group's members to one target version and detect pre-existing divergence — have zero call sites in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/`. Live repro: a fixed group with one already-released member (tagged `1.0.0`) and one never-released member, with a changeset only on the released one, produces `1.0.1` and `0.1.1` on disk after `callisto version` — two different version numbers in the same "fixed" group, exit 0, zero diagnostics. A stronger repro with both members already divergently released produced the same silent pass-through where the spec explicitly requires a hard `FixedGroupDivergent` error. *Category: correctness — see also the closely related finding below, which reproduces the same defect from the live cascade path rather than the dead-code side.*

**Fixed-group members resolve to independent target versions from the live, wired cascade path.** Reported independently from a Cargo-workspace scenario: `bump_target` in `cascade.rs` computes each fixed-group sibling's target from its *own* prior on-disk version rather than a group-wide aligned target — the severity is unioned correctly across the group, but the resulting version numbers are not. Two members ended up at `2.0.0` and `1.0.1` after the same version run. Because this is on the default, unconditionally-reachable code path (no feature flag), this is a live, silent, compounding data-integrity bug in the core versioning engine — every subsequent release widens the drift further, with no self-correction. *This and the item above trace to the same root cause (`bump_target` never delegating to `fixed_group_target`); logging both because they were surfaced from independent scenarios and both carry standalone repro evidence.*

### High (10)

**`callisto tag` fabricates a `sha` when a tag exists at a mismatched commit.** Requesting a tag that already exists but points elsewhere returns `exit 0` with a `CreatedTag.sha` equal to the *requested* sha, not the tag's real target — actively wrong output, not just a missing field. A stronger, fully organic repro (no hand-edited JSON) via a real `plan-publish` → `tag --floating-major` sequence, matching the exact invocation in `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`, showed the same misreport for a floating major tag. The spec explicitly requires this to be a hard error diagnostic. *Category: correctness.*

**One malformed changeset file hides every other pending changeset in the workspace.** A single `.changeset/*.md` with an empty summary aborts `status`, `validate`, `version`, and `compose-pr-body` with only the raw parse error — even with valid, unrelated changesets present alongside it, none of which are mentioned. Worse, the same root cause degrades in the opposite (silent) direction on `plan-publish`: with the malformed file present, the command still exits 0 but plans against stale, unbumped versions, which a CI pipeline would then tag and attempt to (re-)publish. *Category: usability / silent fallback.*

**Manifest discovery silently drops any file that fails to parse or read.** A syntactically broken `pyproject.toml` (confirmed for all three ecosystems by extension) simply vanishes from the workspace — `status` and `validate` report success, `validate` says `valid: true`, and in one scenario `version` reported "No pending changesets found" while a real pending changeset for the invisible package sat unprocessed. The spec explicitly names this exact failure mode and mandates loud failure. *Category: correctness.*

**The `inference` (conventional-commits severity) feature is never enabled anywhere real builds happen.** Default builds, `just ci`, every GitHub workflow, and — critically — `.github/actions/setup-callisto/action.yml`'s real build/install path all use default features, which exclude `inference`. Rebuilding with `--features inference` against an identical repo with unprocessed breaking-change commits correctly computed a major bump (`0.1.0 → 1.0.0`); the default binary reported zero bumps. The spec's own milestone table places this feature at v0.2 as default-on; the workspace is at 0.3.3. *Category: correctness.*

**The pre-release-cursor mechanism is fully implemented and completely unwired.** `resolve_pre_cursor`/`advance_pre_cursor` have zero callers outside their own tests; `TagIndex::build` unconditionally inserts `None` for every package's cursor. Live repro (inference feature on): a pre-release cycle followed by a second `version --dry-run` re-counted an already-consumed commit, producing `commits: 3` where the correct pre-cursor-scoped window would have been 2 commits and a lower severity. *Category: correctness (gated behind the non-default `inference` feature).*

**Commit inference's pathspecs target the manifest file, not the package directory.** `aggregate.rs` builds inference pathspecs from each manifest's literal file path (`crates/pkg-3/Cargo.toml`) instead of its parent directory. Live repro: a `fix:` commit touching only `crates/core/src/lib.rs` was completely invisible to inference; the identical commit touching `Cargo.toml` directly was correctly detected. This makes the feature a near-total no-op for real source commits in any normal package layout. *Severity recalibrated from the original Critical claim to High, since `inference` is not a default feature. Category: correctness.*

**Two unrelated packages sharing a name across ecosystems fail to load the entire workspace.** Every discovered package ID is constructed as ecosystem-agnostic `PackageId::Bare`, so a Cargo crate and an unrelated npm package that happen to share a name — in different directories — produce `E100: defined at multiple paths` and block every command for the whole workspace. This includes the standard maturin/PyO3 layout (a Rust crate and its Python binding, same name, sibling directories) — a deliberate, common shape, not an edge case. *Category: correctness.*

**`IdentityIndex.prefixed` is dead code, making documented ecosystem-prefixed group-member spellings always fail.** The `cargo:foo` / `npm:foo` spellings the spec documents as valid group-member addressing always hard-fail with a false "not found in workspace" error, because the lookup map they depend on is never populated. (Discovered as a byproduct of re-verifying the discrepancy in §2.3.) *Category: correctness.*

**`apply_version_plan` has no transaction boundary.** A failure partway through a multi-package apply (I/O error, or the existing `UnexpectedManifestVersion` drift check) leaves already-written manifests on disk, unstaged, with the error message naming only the failing package. Reproduced with both a permission-denied write and an organic version-mismatch trigger; in both cases prior packages were silently mutated with no rollback and no mention in the error. Re-running after fixing the cause silently double-bumped the already-written package. *Category: correctness.*

**`main.rs`'s own documented exit-code contract for `status --check` contradicts the implemented behavior.** The in-source comment table says exit 0 means "no errors and at least one pending changeset"; the real implementation returns 1 for that case. This is the root cause underlying the critical release-pipeline finding above. *Severity recalibrated up from the original Medium claim to High, since the shipped action implements the stale documented contract verbatim. Category: output-contract.*

### Medium (5)

**`GraphError::ParseChangeset` drops real diagnostic codes and help text.** Unlike nearly every sibling error variant, it carries no `#[diagnostic]` attribute, so a changeset with a real, actionable error (e.g. `E055` empty summary, with help text already written in the codebase) surfaces in both JSON and text output as a bare `callisto::error` with no code and `help: null`. Verified across all 11 `ParseError` variants and across `status`, `validate`, `version`, and `compose-pr-body`.

**A pyproject.toml-only workspace cannot be located as a workspace root.** `is_workspace_root` recognizes exactly four markers (Cargo `[workspace]`, npm `workspaces`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `.moon/`), none Python-aware, despite pyproject.toml being a fully wired, default-on ecosystem elsewhere in the same codebase. The only workaround is creating an unrelated empty `.moon/` directory; even `callisto init` cannot bootstrap past this.

**`callisto schema`'s generated schema for `PackageId`/`Version` doesn't match the real wire format.** `#[schemars(with = "String")]` on these types is a documented-but-silent no-op at the container level in the schemars version in use; the generated schema shows the raw enum shape (`{"Bare": "..."}`), while real serialization is a plain string. Hand-authoring a `tag --plan` file per the published schema produces a hard parse failure. Confirmed the real CLI's own JSON output fails validation against its own published schema for 9 of the 10 `schema --type` targets.

**Real moon's `project-graph --json` output keys its `data` map by numeric graph-node index, not by project ID — the opposite of what code comments and test fixtures assert.** Current code is correct today because it never reads the map's own keys, but the invariant is actively mis-documented in two places, all four existing test fixtures use the wrong (id-keyed) shape, and a mutation test proved a plausible "simplification" refactor (`graph.data.get(&dep.id)`) would silently break dependency-edge resolution on real moon output while every existing test still passes.

**`dry_run::assert_no_disk_mutation`'s core safety fixture silently passes on a nonexistent root.** The crate's headline test-invariant harness returns success with no panic when given a root path that doesn't exist on disk, because directory enumeration failures are swallowed into an empty snapshot on both sides of the diff. Confirmed test-only blast radius (no production dependents); every real call site in the codebase happens to use a live `TempDir`, so this is currently latent rather than actively misleading anyone today.

### Low (3)

**`pre exit` on a workspace that never entered pre-release mode returns a generic I/O error.** The codebase already has a well-worded "already exited" message for the mirror-image state; the more common first-time case falls through to a raw `fs::read_to_string` I/O error with misleading "check permissions" help text.

**`ShellGit` strips a commit message's own real trailing newline.** `parse_git_log_output` unconditionally trims all trailing `\n` characters, intending to remove only `git log`'s single format-artifact newline. Any commit whose stored message genuinely ends in a newline (the git default for any body-bearing commit under standard cleanup rules) loses that byte on the shell backend while the native gix backend preserves it exactly, breaking the crate's own documented backend-parity guarantee. Currently latent for production consumers, since the sole downstream parser normalizes trailing whitespace away before it matters.

**Diagnostic error codes are inconsistent.** Some CLI errors surface a stable, numeric catalog code (`E030`, `E111`); many equally common, user-facing conditions (bad `--type` value, bad `--cwd`, unknown package, malformed plan JSON) fall back to a generic `callisto::error` / `callisto::io_error` string that collapses 21+ distinct conditions into one value, indistinguishable to any consumer branching on `error.code`. No error-code catalog exists anywhere in the repo to make this a broken promise, so the harm is namespace incoherence rather than documentation drift.

## 4. Performance Findings

All timings below were measured with the release binary against synthetic git repositories built fresh under scratch directories, never against the real repository.

| # | Finding | Category | Severity (calibrated) |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `callisto status` walks the *entire* reachable repo history for every package instead of stopping at each package's own tag | Superlinear scaling | High *(down from claimed Critical)* |
| P2 | `TagIndex::build` recompiles a glob matcher and rescans the full tag list once per package | Superlinear scaling | Medium *(up from claimed Low)* |
| P3 | Cargo workspace-inherited dependency rewrites bypass batching — N separate open/parse/fsync/rename cycles against one file | Redundant I/O | Medium *(down from claimed High)* |
| P4 | The workspace-root `Cargo.toml` is read and parsed up to 3× per command; one of those reads is provably discarded work | Redundant I/O | Low *(down from claimed Medium)* |
| P5 | `commits_since_with_pathspec` always performs two full unbounded revwalks per package, regardless of tag proximity to HEAD | Superlinear scaling | High |
| P6 | With `inference` enabled, severity inference runs for every package regardless of `release_trigger`, using file-level (not directory-level) pathspecs | Superlinear scaling | High |
| P7 | Native gix and shelled-git backends have inverted, undocumented scaling shapes; gix already ships an unused bounded-walk API that fixes both | Other | Medium |
| P8 | Every npm `package.json` is read+parsed 3× per graph build; every `Cargo.toml` 2× | Redundant I/O | Low *(down from claimed Medium)* |

**P1/P5** were surfaced independently by two investigative lanes and trace to the same root cause: `GitDataSource::commits_since_with_pathspec` does two unbounded `rev_walk(...).all()` passes (one from HEAD, one from the `since` tag) and filters post-hoc, rather than bounding the walk itself. Measured on a controlled 100-package fixture with history depth varied independently of package count: cost tracked total repo history, not commits-since-tag, confirmed by a tag-removed baseline that stayed flat while the tagged version grew linearly with history depth. At a realistic shape (100 packages, 50,001-commit history, tags 5 commits behind HEAD), `status` took ~2.05s versus ~13ms for the identical repo with tags removed — over 99% wasted revwalk. A correctness symptom rides along: the cheap short-circuit this triggers reports `changedSinceLastTag: true` for every package on any repo-wide commit since its tag, even when the change touched no file in that package's own directory, so the expensive walk is also computing a wrong answer. *Original "superlinear in package count" framing was a harness artifact — corrected: scaling is linear in package count and linear in total history, i.e. bilinear, not superlinear-in-N.*

**P2** — `matching_tags` compiles a fresh `globset::Glob` and does a full linear scan of the entire tag list per package. Measured directly: at 1,000 packages / 41,000 tags, this costs ~640ms of wasted user CPU, closely matched by an isolated `globset` replica (predicted 661ms). A `GlobSet`-based single-pass fix, verified to produce byte-identical package selection, measured 357–798× faster at the tested scales.

**P3** — `WorkspaceCargoResolver`-routed writes for `[workspace.dependencies]` bypass the crate's existing batched-write optimization by design (a deliberately deferred non-goal from a prior spec, not an unnoticed gap), producing one full atomic-write-with-fsync cycle per rewritten dependency entry sharing the same root manifest. Interposer-instrumented run confirmed 8 `rename()` calls against one file for 8 rewritten entries in a single `callisto version` invocation; controlled A/B measured a clean linear cost of ~15–25ms per redundant entry.

**P4** — three near-identical code paths (`ManifestWalkResolver::build`, `Workspace::base_versions`, `apply_version_plan`'s prelude) each independently re-read and re-parse the workspace-root `Cargo.toml`. One of the three (`base_versions`) does so purely to build a value that is provably discarded by the manifest cache it feeds. Measured cost scales with root-manifest size, not package count: ~90µs on this repo's own manifest, up to ~3.9ms on a pathological 90KB/1,010-dependency root — real but small in absolute terms at typical scale.

**P6** — with the non-default `inference` feature on, `aggregate()` calls severity inference for every package unconditionally, never checking `pkg.release_trigger` (which exists specifically to gate this). Measured 12–24× slowdown versus the default-features binary on identical repos, growing to over 1 second at 40 packages / 501 commits. A correctness defect compounds this: with the file-path (not directory) pathspec bug, essentially all of that cost computes zero signal — verified end-to-end with a real source commit that inference failed to detect at all.

**P7** — the shelled-git fallback uses git's own bounded range syntax (flat cost regardless of history depth); the native gix path always walks full history (linear cost). At this audit's tested scale native still wins in absolute terms, but the crossover was measured directly at roughly 1,250 commits without a commit-graph file present. More importantly, gix already exposes a bounded/hidden-tip walk API (`rev_walk(...).with_hidden(...)`) that was measured at ~60× faster than the shell fallback and ~2,400× faster than the current native path at 50,000 commits — an available, unused fix.

**P8** — `detect_npm_role` and the manifest-cache open path each independently re-read and re-parse every npm `package.json` (not just napi platform packages, as originally scoped — the redundancy applies to every npm package in the workspace). Measured 11–13% of total command wall time at 150+ npm packages; below the process-startup floor at the originally-claimed scale of 10–15 platform packages, hence the severity downgrade. The same root cause costs roughly 2× as much per package for `Cargo.toml` (toml_edit parse is ~18× more expensive than the JSON parse it's paired with), which the original claim didn't scope in.

## 5. Scope and Limits

- All reproductions ran against the real, compiled `callisto` binary (`target/debug` or `target/release`, rebuilt at current HEAD as needed) in throwaway git repositories under scratch directories — the tracked working tree was never modified by this audit, and every session verified `git status` clean before and after.
- The `inference` Cargo feature gates several of the confirmed findings (P6, and the new-issue findings on pre-cursor and pathspec scoping). It is not enabled in any default build or shipped install path today, which bounds current production exposure for that subset even though the defects are real and reachable once the feature is turned on.
- Performance timings are order-of-magnitude and shape evidence from synthetic repos sized for clear signal, not production capacity planning; several severities were revised after direct measurement replaced the original estimate, in both directions (up for P2/P17, down for P1/P3/P4/P8) — treat the calibrated severities in this report, not the originally claimed ones, as current.
- This pass did not re-run the full 115-item static ledger — only the critical/high subset (59 items) was validated live, plus a fresh sweep for runtime-only and performance issues. Medium/low static findings were not re-verified here.
- One static finding required a second, more careful runtime attempt to resolve correctly (§2.3); that discrepancy is the clearest evidence in this report that a single negative repro should not be treated as proof of unreachability without deliberately trying to construct the reachable path.

content.content:
Critical3

callisto status --check's exit-code contract is inverted in the shipped release pipeline.

The compiled CLI's real --check contract (confirmed by both the binary's own behavior and its unit tests) is: exit 1 when changesets are pending, exit 2 when none are pending — it never returns 0. The shipped .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml branches on -eq 0 for "has pending changesets" and treats anything else but 2 as a hard failure. Live repro: with a real pending changeset, running the action's verbatim bash block against the real binary printed ::error::callisto status --check failed with exit code 1 and hard-exited the step — the "create/update the release PR" path is unreachable in every real run where it should fire. A second, independently-discovered defect compounds this: clap's own usage-error exit code (2) collides with the "no changesets pending" branch, so a CLI argument typo is silently reinterpreted as "workspace clean" and falls into the publish path — fail-open on an irreversible operation.

correctness / output-contract.

Fixed-group safety checks are fully built, unit-tested, and never called from any real command.

pre_mutation_checks, fixed_group_target, and napi_drift — the functions that force-align a fixed group's members to one target version and detect pre-existing divergence — have zero call sites in crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/. Live repro: a fixed group with one already-released member (tagged 1.0.0) and one never-released member, with a changeset only on the released one, produces 1.0.1 and 0.1.1 on disk after callisto version — two different version numbers in the same "fixed" group, exit 0, zero diagnostics. A stronger repro with both members already divergently released produced the same silent pass-through where the spec explicitly requires a hard FixedGroupDivergent error.

correctness — see also the closely related finding below, which reproduces the same defect from the live cascade path rather than the dead-code side.

Fixed-group members resolve to independent target versions from the live, wired cascade path.

--
High10

callisto tag fabricates a sha when a tag exists at a mismatched commit.

Requesting a tag that already exists but points elsewhere returns exit 0 with a CreatedTag.sha equal to the requested sha, not the tag's real target — actively wrong output, not just a missing field. A stronger, fully organic repro (no hand-edited JSON) via a real plan-publish → tag --floating-major sequence, matching the exact invocation in .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml, showed the same misreport for a floating major tag. The spec explicitly requires this to be a hard error diagnostic.

correctness.

One malformed changeset file hides every other pending changeset in the workspace.

A single .changeset/*.md with an empty summary aborts status, validate, version, and compose-pr-body with only the raw parse error — even with valid, unrelated changesets present alongside it, none of which are mentioned. Worse, the same root cause degrades in the opposite (silent) direction on plan-publish: with the malformed file present, the command still exits 0 but plans against stale, unbumped versions, which a CI pipeline would then tag and attempt to (re-)publish.

usability / silent fallback.
=== perf table ===

All timings below were measured with the release binary against synthetic git repositories built fresh under scratch directories, never against the real repository.

#FindingCategorySeverity (calibrated)
P1callisto status walks the entire reachable repo history for every package instead of stopping at each package's own tagSuperlinear scalingHigh (down from claimed Critical)
P2TagIndex::build recompiles a glob matcher and rescans the full tag list once per packageSuperlinear scalingMedium (up from claimed Low)
P3Cargo workspace-inherited dependency rewrites bypass batching — N separate open/parse/fsync/rename cycles against one fileRedundant I/OMedium (down from claimed High)
P4The workspace-root Cargo.toml is read and parsed up to 3× per command; one of those reads is provably discarded workRedundant I/OLow (down from claimed Medium)
P5commits_since_with_pathspec always performs two full unbounded revwalks per package, regardless of tag proximity to HEADSuperlinear scalingHigh
P6With inference enabled, severity inference runs for every package regardless of release_trigger, using file-level (not directory-level) pathspecsSuperlinear scalingHigh
P7Native gix and shelled-git backends have inverted, undocumented scaling shapes; gix already ships an unused bounded-walk API that fixes bothOtherMedium
P8Every npm package.json is read+parsed 3× per graph build; every Cargo.toml 2×Redundant I/OLow (down from claimed Medium)

P1/P5 were surfaced independently by two investigative lanes and trace to the same root cause: GitDataSource::commits_since_with_pathspec does two unbounded rev_walk(...).all() passes (one from HEAD, one from the since tag) and filters post-hoc, rather than bounding the walk itself. Measured on a controlled 100-package fixture with history depth varied independently of package count: cost tracked total repo history, not commits-since-tag, confirmed by a tag-removed baseline that stayed flat while the tagged version grew linearly with history depth. At a realistic shape (100 packages, 50,001-commit history, tags 5 commits behind HEAD), status took ~2.05s versus ~13ms for the identical repo with tags removed — over 99% wasted revwalk. A correctness symptom rides along: the cheap short-circuit this triggers reports changedSinceLastTag: true for every package on any repo-wide commit since its tag, even when the change touched no file in that package's own directory, so the expensive walk is also computing a wrong answer. Original "superlinear in package count" framing was a harness artifact — corrected: scaling is linear in package count and linear in total history, i.e. bilinear, not superlinear-in-N.

P2 — matching_tags compiles a fresh globset::Glob and does a full linear scan of the entire tag list per package. Measured directly: at 1,000 packages / 41,000 tags, this costs ~640ms of wasted user CPU, closely matched by an isolated globset replica (predicted 661ms). A GlobSet-based single-pass fix, verified to produce byte-identical package selection, measured 357–798× faster at the tested scales.

--

**[Callisto Drift Audit](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/42673b56-d387-4e58-a8b0-44a49e9d42ae)** — updated in place, same URL. Now a single combined report: 3-way severity charts, a Pass filter (Static/Runtime new/Performance) crossed with the existing Severity filter, and all three passes in one place.

**What the runtime+perf pass found:**

- **56 of 59 critical/high static findings reproduced live** — real command, real workspace, real output. 2 were pure code-facts. 1 produced a discrepancy — and this is the most important result in the whole report: a first-pass runtime attempt tested one scenario, got a clean result, and over-generalized it into "this bug is unreachable." The Opus verify stage caught that, found the actual reachable path within minutes, and reproduced an even worse consequence live: a fixed group silently and permanently drifting apart in version number, with real numbers on disk to prove it.
- **21 new runtime-only issues**, 3 critical — most notably: **the shipped GitHub Action's exit-code contract is inverted**, meaning the release-PR path is unreachable in every real run where it should fire; and **fixed groups can drift apart in version number** even through the normally-wired cascade path, not just the dead-code side.
- **8 performance findings**, with real measured numbers — the standout is `callisto status` doing two full unbounded git revwalks per package regardless of tag proximity: **~2.05s vs ~13ms** on a 100-package/50k-commit synthetic repo, over 99% wasted work, plus a correctness bug riding along (it also computes the wrong "changed since last tag" answer for unrelated files).

Same as before — I don't think it's my call to start fixing any of this unilaterally. Given the shape of what's here (a genuine release-pipeline breakage, a data-integrity bug in the version engine, and a real perf issue with a known fix already available in the `gix` API), where do you want to start?

and the separate `WorkspaceCargoResolver` type), user chose the lowest-risk of three options —
exclude any physical file receiving writes through both mechanisms from batching entirely, rather
than reordering writes or extending Spec A's mutate/persist split to `WorkspaceCargoResolver` too.
Implementation: `classify_manifest_writes`/`ManifestWriteGroup`/`ManifestWriteClassification`
(new, `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`) partition a plan's Manifest-trait-routed writes into
per-path batchable groups and a mixed-routing exclusion set via a full pre-scan; `apply_version_plan`
opens each batchable path's manifest exactly once, applies its bump (same skip/write/error
precondition as before) then its rewrites in order, and persists exactly once — processing groups
strictly sequentially (one path fully persisted-or-errored before the next handle opens) to prevent
the stale-handle-clobber hazard. `persist_call_count`/`reset_persist_call_count` added to
`callisto-manifests` mirroring the existing `open_call_count` precedent.
Both the spec (5 drafting/audit rounds, canon-exit-gate passed on retry 2) and the plan (7
vector-challenger rounds) went through unusually heavy adversarial review before implementation —
real bugs caught each round, including a silent-data-loss ambiguity in the persist-trigger condition,
a self-contradictory test fixture, an unconstructible acceptance criterion, a dishonest red-phase
waiver, and flaky process-global-counter tests.
Exit-gate: PASS (high confidence). All 18 AC verified fresh from disk/code. `just ci` full 7-phase
suite green (766 tests, up from 751) plus `--all-features` prechecks on both touched crates.
Mutation-tested at the gate (cargo-mutants run directly by the gate, same as Spec A): 12/13 mutants
caught; the one survivor (a hardcoded `persist_call_count()`) closed with a follow-up precision test.
Core safety property (strict per-group sequential processing, preventing the original spec's
stale-handle-clobber bug) confirmed both by code trace and by killed mutants on the exclusion guards.
Commits: d2b1014 (persist_call_count) through c880280 (T13 evidence correction), c661b38 (mutation
gap closed), a739773/7346f48 (spec/plan committed).

### Post-Track-G: full workspace audit + 8-bug remediation — DONE (see SESSION_HANDOFF.md)

Full adversarial audit (8-dimension, 24-agent workflow) found 3 critical + 7 high confirmed bugs,
concentrated almost entirely in pre-existing code committed early this session (`e0cc091`, `60e0bef`)
that never went through canon→vector→lambda — NOT in Track F/G's own freshly-built code. All 8
confirmed critical/high findings fixed via strict TDD, commits `bca04b1` through `def6862`.
Report: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/80f347f5-afea-488c-886b-518bea99a458
**See `.claude/plans/SESSION_HANDOFF.md` for full detail and the recommended next step** (4 named
test-coverage gaps + 41 unverified medium/low findings as backlog).

**Process lesson from this incident** (saved to memory, read it):
code found already-written in a dirty working tree gets the SAME rigor as freshly-written code —
"compiles + existing tests pass" is not verification. See
`feedback_found_code_needs_same_rigor.md` in the memory index.

---

## Pipeline Protocol (follow for every track, in order)

1. `canon:canon-drafter` — write spec@1 to `.claude/specs/`
2. `canon:canon-auditor` — must pass before continuing
3. `canon:canon-exit-gate` — must pass before continuing
4. `vector:vector-planner` — produce plan@1 with exact red tests
5. `vector:vector-challenger` — must pass before continuing
6. `lambda:lambda-recon` — confirm baseline tests pass
7. `lambda:lambda-implementer` — one task at a time, red phase MANDATORY
8. `lambda:lambda-reviewer` — review each commit before next task
9. `lambda:lambda-exit-gate` — adversarial final check
10. `just ci` — must exit 0

Constraints:
- NEVER commit without explicit user instruction
- NEVER invoke `callisto publish` against any real registry
- Confirm test FAILS before writing implementation
- Do not interleave Track B and Track E implementation tasks

input.description: Cross-reference semantic model and prior audit
input.prompt:
Read-only research task in the Rust workspace at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto. I'm building a remediation plan for a large set of newly-found bugs/gaps (144 items from a fresh audit: 115 static spec-vs-code gaps, 21 new runtime-only issues, 8 performance findings) and need to ground it against this project's existing planning conventions and a PRIOR audit from an earlier session.

1. Read all 4 files in `.claude/semantic-model/`: `core-identity.md`, `version-flow.md`, `config-resolution.md`, `error-taxonomy.md`. Summarize each one's scope in 2-3 sentences: what invariants/design decisions does it document, and which of these general problem areas does it cover: (a) PackageId/Ecosystem/identity resolution, (b) VersionPlan/apply_version_plan/idempotency, (c) config resolution ([[package]]/[[package-set]] matching, specificity), (d) GraphError/ConfigError taxonomy and E-codes.

2. Read `~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/memory/project_workspace_audit_2026-08.md` (the memory file summarizing a PRIOR full workspace audit from 2026-08-12, referenced in `.claude/plans/SESSION_HANDOFF.md`). That prior audit found 3 critical + 7 high bugs (all fixed, see `.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md`'s "Post-Track-G" section for the list) plus 41 unverified medium/low findings that were NEVER addressed. Summarize: what were the 41 unverified findings about (by theme/category), and does the memory file give enough detail (file:line, description) that I could cross-check whether any of them overlap with a NEW finding? List any theme overlaps you can spot with these NEW-audit themes: (a) fixed-group version alignment/divergence, (b) callisto-cli's dependency on callisto-manifests, (c) release-pipeline/GitHub Action JSON contract mismatches, (d) DependencyResolver trait misplacement, (e) manifest/config fixture test-infrastructure gaps, (f) performance (redundant I/O, git operations).

3. Also check: does `.claude/specs/` contain any existing SPEC-xxx.json files whose scope might already cover part of what I'm about to plan (e.g. a spec about identity resolution, config resolution, or apply_version_plan that's already drafted but maybe not fully implemented)? List filenames and one-line descriptions of any found.

Report back concisely (under 500 words): the 4 semantic-model file summaries, the 41-findings theme summary with any overlap flags, and the specs/ inventory. This is pure research -- don't propose fixes or a plan, just report what you find.

input.description: Verify root-cause groupings for remediation plan
input.prompt:
Read-only research task in the Rust workspace at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto (crate: callisto-graph mainly). I'm grouping a large list of confirmed audit findings into coherent remediation "tracks" by shared root cause, and need to verify whether several clusters I suspect are related really do share one underlying fix, or need separate independent fixes. Read the actual current code (not just my descriptions) to answer each question below.

**Cluster A — fixed-group version engine.** Read `crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs`'s `bump_target` function in full, `crates/callisto-graph/src/groups.rs`'s `fixed_group_target` and `pre_mutation_checks` functions in full, and grep the whole `callisto-graph` crate for call sites of `fixed_group_target`, `pre_mutation_checks`, and `napi_drift` (outside their own definitions/tests). Question: are these three functions (fixed_group_target, pre_mutation_checks, napi_drift) all unwired for the SAME reason (e.g. nothing in `commands/version.rs` or `apply.rs` ever calls the right entry point), or are they three structurally separate gaps needing three separate fixes? Also check: does `GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership` (grep `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs`'s `GroupTable::resolve`) get constructed anywhere, and is fixing THAT the same code change as wiring `bump_target` to `fixed_group_target`, or a separate change in a different function? Give a concrete recommendation: how many distinct fixes does "make fixed-group alignment actually enforced" require, and roughly which functions does each touch?

**Cluster B — identity/ecosystem resolution.** Read `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/pattern.rs`'s `PackagePattern::matches`/`matches_in_ecosystems`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs` around line 349 (where `[[package]] match` gets parsed), `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs`'s `IgnoreWalkLocator::projects()` (full method), and `crates/callisto-graph/src/identity.rs`'s `IdentityIndex` struct plus `resolve_native_with_fallback`. Questions: (1) Is "[[package]]/[[package-set]] match compared against package NAME instead of workspace-relative PATH" (in pattern.rs/resolve.rs) the same underlying code path as "IgnoreWalkLocator never filters by Cargo [workspace] members/exclude or npm workspaces globs" (in ignore_walk.rs), or are these two independent gaps in different functions that each need their own fix? (2) Is "IdentityIndex.prefixed is never populated" related to or independent from "resolve_native_with_fallback silently falls back cross-ecosystem"? (3) Would fixing package-name validation (rejecting a manifest-declared name that happens to be prefix-parseable, e.g. an npm package literally named "cargo/foo") at ONE validation point (e.g. wherever `PackageId::parse` or discovery first reads a manifest's name field) resolve both the "IdentityIndex.prefixed dead code" issue AND the "two same-named packages across ecosystems block the whole workspace" issue, or are those genuinely separate? Give a concrete recommendation: how many distinct fixes does "harden identity/ecosystem resolution" require, and which functions does each touch?

**Cluster C — is platform-manifest/optionalDependencies writes (§7.6 steps 4-5, `apply.rs` never references `platform_writes`/`optional_dep_updates`) part of the same code area as Cluster A (fixed-group), or an independent gap in a different part of `apply_version_plan`?** Read `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` in full to answer.

Report back concisely (under 600 words), structured by cluster (A, B, C), each with a clear numbered list of "this needs N separate fixes: (1) touches function X because Y, (2) touches function Z because W, ..." Don't propose full solutions, just the minimal-fix-boundary analysis so I can scope tracks correctly. Read-only -- do not edit anything.

- **config-resolution.md** (`config/resolve.rs`, `config/pattern.rs`, `walk.rs`): Documents `ResolvedConfig`/`PackageConfig`/`PackagePattern` and the two-step `[[package]]` → `[[package-set]]` resolution with the Track E specificity order (Prefixed `[[package]]` > Bare `[[package]]` > `[[package-set]]` glob > manifest defaults), plus the cross-ecosystem diagnostic. Covers **(c)**.
- **error-taxonomy.md** (`callisto-graph/src/error.rs`): Full `GraphError`/`ConfigError` E-code table plus conventions (transparent variants, `#[non_exhaustive]`, no per-variant `result_large_err`). Notably documents that E113 (`InvalidChangelogPath`) was **previously mis-numbered E117**, colliding with `UnexpectedManifestVersion`, and has since been renumbered — and separately flags three `ConfigError` variants (`PackageMatchedNothing`, `PackageSetMatchedNothing`, `OverlappingPackageSets`) as defined but **never emitted**. Important: `SESSION_HANDOFF.md` (written 2026-08-12) frames the 41 as an untouched backlog. **Theme overlap flags vs. your new-audit categories:**
- **(a) fixed-group version alignment/divergence** — no direct hit, but task #31 (`IdentityIndex.platform` never populated → `napi_drift` group-member comparison always empty) is adjacent (group-membership wiring, not version divergence). Worth checking your new findings against #31 specifically.
- **(b) callisto-cli → callisto-manifests dependency direction** — no matching architecture-direction finding in the 41; only incidental co-mentions.
- **(c) release-pipeline/GitHub Action JSON contract mismatches** — no hits at all in the 41; likely genuinely new territory.
- **(d) DependencyResolver trait misplacement** — no exact match, but #13 ("Resolve `IdentityResolver` duplication — delete if dead, else route through `Manifest` trait") is the closest analog (different resolver name, same duplication/misplacement pattern) — flag for cross-check.
- **(e) manifest/config fixture test-infrastructure gaps** — #15 (Layer-1 AGPL `callisto-fixtures` dev-dependency) is adjacent but about licensing, not fixture coverage gaps per se.
- **(f) performance (redundant I/O, git ops)** — strong overlap; #16, #17, #18, #32, #33 are marked completed and #41 is still pending (same redundancy class, latent/unwired code).

Detail level is sufficient for cross-checking (each task has file:line-level description), but it's a flat task list, not indexed by file — you'd need to grep it per new finding.

## 3. `.claude/specs/` inventory

- `SPEC-APPLY-BATCH-002.json` — apply_version_plan write-batching/grouping (Spec B). **DONE.**
- `SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001.json` — Manifest trait mutate/persist split (Spec A). **DONE.**
- `track-b-idempotent-apply.json` — idempotent `apply_version_plan` (covers **b**). **DONE.**
- `track-e-specificity.json` — `PackageId` specificity + cross-ecosystem diagnostic (covers **a/c**). **DONE.**
- `track-f-resolution-extraction.json` — `resolve_package_config` extraction, two-pass specificity (covers **c**). **DONE.**
- `track-g-matrix-napi-maturin.json` — `callisto matrix` napi/maturin auto-discovery. **DONE.**
- `callisto-matrix.md` — supporting design doc for Track G (not a JSON spec).

All specs touching identity/config-resolution/apply_version_plan are marked DONE in `ACTIVE.md` — no drafted-but-unimplemented spec currently overlaps your planned scope.</result>

input.prompt:
You're validating a draft remediation plan for the Callisto Rust workspace (release-engine CLI, /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto). A large audit this session found 144 confirmed issues (115 static spec-vs-code gaps, 21 new runtime-only issues confirmed by live reproduction against the compiled binary, 8 performance findings with real measured timings) across all 14 crates. I've grouped them into draft "tracks" by shared root cause and need you to pressure-test the structure: validate boundaries, flag missed cross-track dependencies, and recommend a rigor level per track using this project's OWN established criteria (documented in .claude/plans/ACTIVE.md's "Pipeline Protocol" section — read that file first, along with .claude/plans/SESSION_HANDOFF.md for precedent on how a similar large-audit remediation was previously sequenced and scoped).

This project has two rigor levels in active use: (1) the full canon→vector→lambda SDD pipeline (spec draft → adversarial spec audit → exit gate → plan → adversarial plan challenge → TDD implementation → per-commit review → adversarial exit gate) for substantial "Tracks", used when scope is architecturally significant or blast radius is wide; (2) a lighter TDD loop (red test → minimal fix → green → independent review agent → full test suite + clippy + fmt → commit, one fix at a time, never batching unrelated fixes) for narrower, well-scoped bug fixes. A repo memory note says: "Skip canon ceremony for targeted bug fixes with RED tests already written; canon auditor loops infinitely on implementation-detail prose." Your job includes recommending which tier fits each track below.

Here is my draft track structure (verified against real current code via two prior research passes this session):

**Track 1 — Fixed-group version engine correctness (CRITICAL).** Three separate fixes, all confirmed via direct code reads: (a) `crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs`'s `raise()`/`bump_target` currently bumps each fixed-group sibling independently from its own base version instead of delegating to the already-implemented `fixed_group_target` (in `groups.rs`) for a group-aligned target -- likely needs `CascadeInput` to gain a `tags: &TagIndex` field it doesn't currently have. (b) `pre_mutation_checks` (groups.rs, does divergence-check + calls `napi_drift`) is fully implemented, unit-tested, but has zero call sites anywhere in `commands/version.rs` or `apply.rs` -- needs to be wired into the version command's orchestration before `run_cascade`. (c) `GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership` is declared but `GroupTable::resolve` (config/groups.rs) never detects the case where two differently-spelled raw group-member strings resolve, post-identity, to the same `PackageId` across two different groups -- needs new post-resolution detection logic in `GroupTable::resolve` itself. This was confirmed live: a real repro produced two members of one "fixed" group landing on different version numbers on disk with exit 0 and zero diagnostics; a second, independently-discovered live repro showed the same root cause via the cascade path with real dependency chains, and a third repro showed `ConflictingGroupMembership` is reachable via a prefix-parseable manifest name and produces real, silent, cascading version divergence.

**Track 2 — Platform-manifest / optionalDependencies writes (CRITICAL).** `apply_version_plan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`) never references `plan.platform_writes`/`plan.optional_dep_updates` at all (confirmed: zero matches in the whole file) even though `VersionPlan` carries both fields and the lower-level `Manifest::update_optional_dependencies` trait method is already implemented and tested in `callisto-manifests`. Needs two new write loops in `apply_version_plan`. Independent of Track 1 (confirmed via code read -- different fields, different loops).

**Track 3 — Identity/ecosystem resolution hardening (CRITICAL).** Five separate fixes, all confirmed independent via direct code reads: (a) `[[package]]`/`[[package-set]] match` is compared against a package's NAME (`config/resolve.rs:349`, `config/pattern.rs`) instead of its workspace-relative PATH as both spec docs and the config examples require -- this is a significant semantic change to how `callisto.toml` patterns are interpreted, and I'm flagging it as needing an explicit product decision (does anyone's real config rely on current name-based matching?) before it's spec'd, not just implemented. (b) `IgnoreWalkLocator::projects()` (`locate/ignore_walk.rs`) never filters by Cargo `[workspace]` members/exclude or npm `workspaces`/`pnpm-workspace.yaml` globs at all -- an intentionally-excluded crate (fuzz target, scratch example) gets discovered and treated as a real release-managed package. (c) `IdentityIndex.prefixed` (`identity.rs`) is never populated anywhere in `walk.rs::build`, making the documented `cargo:foo`/`npm:foo` ecosystem-prefixed group-member spelling always fail with a false "not found" error. (d) `walk.rs::build`'s `package_manifest_decls.insert` keys on a name-derived `PackageId` with no ecosystem/path disambiguation, so two unrelated packages in different ecosystems (different directories) sharing a name -- including the standard maturin/PyO3 layout, a Rust crate + its Python binding, same name, sibling dirs -- blocks the ENTIRE workspace with `DuplicatePackage`, confirmed live. (e) `resolve_native_with_fallback` (`identity.rs`) silently falls back to a cross-ecosystem name match when the same-ecosystem lookup misses, contradicting the spec's own worked example ("a Cargo `serde` dependency must not resolve to an npm workspace member called `serde`") -- confirmed still functionally live (not dead code), just wrongly permissive; needs the fallback removed or gated off by default.

**Track 4 — Release-pipeline / CI Action contract correctness (CRITICAL).** Spans `crates/callisto-model` (report types), `crates/callisto-graph` (`commands/tag.rs`, `commands/publish.rs`), AND `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml` (not Rust). Confirmed live: the shipped Action's bash script branches on `-eq 0` for "has pending changesets," but the real compiled binary's `status --check` contract is exit 1 = pending, exit 2 = none pending, never 0 -- the release-PR creation path is unreachable in every real run where it should fire. A second compounding bug: clap's own usage-error exit code (2) collides with the "no changesets pending" branch, so a CLI typo is silently reinterpreted as "workspace clean" and falls into the publish path. Separately, `callisto tag` returns exit 0 with a fabricated `sha` (the requested one, not the tag's real target) when a tag already exists at a different commit -- confirmed via both a hand-built repro and a fully organic `plan-publish` -> `tag --floating-major` sequence matching the Action's real invocation. And `plan_publish` never reads CHANGELOG.md back via the already-implemented `extract_section`, so `ReleaseEntry.changelog_section` is always `None`. Needs coordinated Rust-side + Action-script-side fixes since they're interdependent (can't fix the binary's contract without updating the Action, and vice versa).

**Track 5 — Changelog/PR-body rendering consolidation (HIGH).** `commands/pr_body.rs` never calls `callisto_changelog::render_section` at all (spec's "one render function, three consumers" decision violated) -- builds its own hand-rolled Markdown instead. `ChangeSource::Commit` (inference-driven bumps) and `ChangeSource::NewGroupMember` (fixed-group new-member joins) are both never constructed anywhere in production -- inference bumps get a generic "Version bump (severity)" line instead of itemized commits, and new-group-member joins never render at all. NOTE: fixing `ChangeSource::NewGroupMember` properly likely DEPENDS on Track 1(b) (wiring `pre_mutation_checks`/the group force-set logic that would actually produce a `BumpReason::NewGroupMember` in the first place) -- flag if you agree this creates a sequencing dependency Track 5 should wait on. Also: `ChangelogInput.entries` never unions multiple contributing causes for one package in one run (changeset + cascade + peer-escalation for the same bump silently drops all but the changeset-sourced entries).

**Track 6 — JSON report-contract alignment (callisto-model) (CRITICAL/HIGH mix).** `StatusReport`, `StatusPackageRecord`, `SnapshotReport`, `ComposePrBodyReport`, `CreatedTag`, `InitReport`, `ValidateReport` all have field-shape mismatches against the documented wire contract (missing fields, renamed fields changing the JSON key, wrong optionality). This is mostly mechanical but changes the JSON wire format, which is a BREAKING CHANGE for any external consumer (the GitHub Action reads several of these) -- needs coordination with Track 4 (same Action script) and an explicit decision on whether/how to version the breaking change (a `schemaVersion` field already exists on these report types). Separately, `callisto-model` (Layer 1, documented as "no I/O") now contains real filesystem I/O (`atomic_write`, moved there in a deliberate prior-session architectural decision per its own commit message) -- I believe this is a stale SPEC CLAIM that should be corrected in docs rather than a code regression to revert (the crate's actual hard invariant per CLAUDE.md is license permissiveness, not "no I/O"), but flag if you disagree.

**Track 7 — Performance: git revwalk bounding & redundant I/O (HIGH).** `GitDataSource::commits_since_with_pathspec` (`callisto-vcs`) does two full unbounded revwalks per package regardless of tag proximity to HEAD -- measured ~2.05s vs ~13ms (same repo, tags removed) at 100 packages/50k commits, over 99% wasted work, plus a correctness bug riding along (wrong `changedSinceLastTag` answer for unrelated-file commits). `gix` already exposes an unused bounded-walk API that a separate measurement showed as ~60x faster. Also: per-package glob recompilation in `TagIndex::build` (measured ~640ms wasted at 1000 packages/41k tags), and several smaller redundant-reparse findings (workspace-root Cargo.toml read 3x per command, npm/cargo manifests re-read 2-3x per graph build). One related finding (Cargo workspace-inherited dependency rewrites bypassing existing write-batching) is explicitly a known, deliberately-deferred prior design decision, not a fresh gap -- exclude it from this track's scope, just note it exists. Two more findings (severity inference running unconditionally regardless of `release_trigger`; pathspecs targeting the manifest file instead of the package directory, making commit inference a near-total no-op) are gated behind the non-default `inference` Cargo feature -- lower production exposure today.

**Track 8 — Manifest/config gaps needing product decisions.** `moon.yml`'s `extensions.callisto` block is documented as the highest-precedence config layer but is never deserialized anywhere -- no YAML dependency exists in `callisto-graph` at all. This is either a real feature to build (new dependency, new parsing, real scope) or a spec section that should be cut/deferred -- flag as a decision point. `ConfigError::OverlappingPackageSets`/`PackageMatchedNothing` are declared but never constructed (small, mechanical fix). A pyproject.toml-only workspace can't even be located as a workspace root (`is_workspace_root` has no Python-aware marker) despite Python being a fully-wired, default-on, well-tested ecosystem elsewhere in the same codebase -- and separately, the spec's own claim that Python support is "demand-gated, not implemented" is itself just stale (I believe code should stay as-is and the spec should be corrected, given it's a complete 1681-line implementation with 50+ tests already shipped and default-on).

**Track 9 — Cascade correctness: peer-escalation & cross-ecosystem rewrite keys (CRITICAL).** `cascade_action`'s peer-dependency escalation ignores the true cascading severity (`_source: Severity`, unused parameter) -- every out-of-range peer edge escalates to Major even when the real upstream change was only Patch, with `peer_escalation = true` the documented default. Separately, dependency-spec rewrite keys are built from `PackageId::name()` instead of `IdentityIndex::native_name`, so cross-ecosystem rewrites onto a dual-identity (napi-style) package target the wrong manifest key -- confirmed live, crashes `callisto version` outright on an ordinary Cargo+npm co-located package. Both are scoped, single-function fixes in `cascade.rs`, not architecturally sprawling like Tracks 1/3.

**Track 10 — Test/fixture infrastructure buildout (MEDIUM/LOW production risk, HIGH nominal severity).** `callisto-fixtures` is missing `GraphBuilder`/`ScenarioBuilder`/`ReplayCommandRunner`/the entire vendored `data/` corpus the spec describes as this crate's core purpose -- several crates duplicate ad hoc local test doubles instead. Several crates lack any wasm32-wasip1 CI job despite spec claims. This is large, additive, doesn't affect shipped correctness -- candidate for explicit deferral, matching this project's own precedent (`SESSION_HANDOFF.md` treated an analogous 41-item medium/low backlog as "not a to-do-tonight list" needing explicit user scoping, not silent inclusion).

**Track 11/12 — Diagnostic/error-contract polish + remaining doc-only fixes (LOW).** Smaller mechanical items: missing `#[diagnostic]` attrs on `ParseChangeset`, inconsistent error-code coverage (21+ conditions collapsed to generic codes), stale Cargo.toml diagrams in spec docs, wrong spec section citations. Batch-friendly, low risk.

**Cross-cutting decision flagged separately:** the `inference` Cargo feature (conventional-commit severity inference, just wired into the CLI this session for the first time) is not enabled in any default build/CI/install path today. A real pathspec bug found this session (targets the manifest file, not the package directory) makes it "a near-total no-op for real source commits" regardless -- that bug should be fixed regardless of the default-on question, but whether `inference` becomes default-on (matching its own v0.2 milestone claim) is a separate product decision, not bundled into any track above.

Your job: (1) Read `.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md` and `.claude/plans/SESSION_HANDOFF.md` in full for this project's own precedent on sequencing/rigor decisions. (2) Validate my track boundaries -- flag anything you think should split further or merge. (3) Identify any cross-track dependencies I haven't already flagged (I've flagged: Track 5 depends on Track 1(b); Track 4 and Track 6 both touch the same Action script and should probably be coordinated or sequenced together). (4) Recommend a rigor tier (full canon->vector->lambda vs. lighter TDD loop) for each track using this project's own stated criteria, and a rough priority/phase ordering across tracks (which should go first given severity + dependency order + risk). (5) Explicitly list every product/architecture decision point across all tracks that needs the user's sign-off BEFORE any spec gets drafted (I've named several inline above -- consolidate and check I haven't missed any).

Return a structured report, not code. This is a planning/validation pass only.
